nodeLabels.Character: the poet and the speakers of Part 3
nodeLabels.Emotion: virtues, vices and states of mind
nodeLabels.PersonalThought: private thoughts, on this device only

threads.title: From loving-kindness to compassion
threads.note: He holds that compassion grows from loving-kindness, which starts with your own people. This follows it outward until it reaches every living thing.

steps.quote: give even their bones for others
steps.why: Loving-kindness shows first in what you won’t keep for yourself.

steps.quote: that warmth brings friendship
steps.why: It doesn’t stay where it began: it makes you warm towards people, and the warmth becomes friendship.

steps.quote: the child that loving-kindness bears
steps.why: Here is the link: compassion is the child that loving-kindness bears.

steps.quote: the wealth among wealth
steps.why: The child is weighed against goods and outranks them, for even the low can have goods.

steps.quote: Flesh is another creature’s wound
steps.why: Compassion now goes past people: it sees a wound where others see food.

steps.quote: tenderness towards every living thing
steps.why: Its full reach: the sages are those who live with tenderness towards every living thing.

threads.title: From a sweet word to a true one
threads.note: Speech is tested step by step: is it sweet, is it from the heart, is it of use, is it straight, does it harm? The last test is truth, and nothing stands above it.

steps.quote: picking unripe fruit when ripe fruit is there
steps.why: The first step is an easy choice: when a sweet word is there, a harsh one is unripe fruit.

steps.quote: sweet words that come from the heart
steps.why: Sweetness on the lips isn’t enough: the word must come from the heart, with the face and eyes agreeing.

steps.quote: say the ones with use
steps.why: A word can be sweet and sincere and still be empty, so the next test is whether it is of use.

steps.quote: speech that does not bend
steps.why: Now the word must be straight, and that depends on what is behind it: no bend within.

steps.quote: speech with no harm in it at all
steps.why: Truthfulness gets its definition, and it isn’t bare fact: it is speech that harms no one.

steps.quote: your own heart will burn you
steps.why: The judge of a lie is inside you: your own heart knows, and your own heart does the burning.

steps.quote: nothing at all is better than truthfulness
steps.why: The book’s verdict: of all it has seen to be true, nothing is better than this.

threads.title: What to do with anger
threads.note: The test comes where you have the power to act on your anger. The book counts what anger costs you, and ends by ranking those who give it up with those who renounce.

steps.quote: holds back anger where it can take effect
steps.why: The test comes first: holding back anger only counts where you have the power to act on it.

steps.quote: kills your smile and your joy
steps.why: The first cost falls inside you, on your own joy, before anyone else is touched.

steps.quote: burns the raft of safety
steps.why: Next it reaches your own people, the raft that would have carried you to safety.

steps.quote: doesn’t give up anger and has no self-command
steps.why: It also leaves you exposed: the man who won’t give up anger is easy for anyone, anywhere.

steps.quote: it is you that anger kills
steps.why: The costs come down to one reason, and it isn’t kindness to others: guard against anger to guard yourself.

steps.quote: holds back anger, learns and keeps restraint
steps.why: Holding it back also opens a way in: righteousness comes looking for such a person.

steps.quote: Those who renounce anger are the equals of renouncers
steps.why: To give up anger is to stand with those who gave up the world.

threads.title: Letting go, step by step
threads.note: Seeing that nothing lasts leads to letting go of attachment, letting go needs something to hold to, and the truth cuts off craving at the seed. This is the order of chapters 34 to 37.

steps.quote: a blade sawing through life
steps.why: Everything begins with seeing: what looks like a day is a blade sawing through life.

steps.quote: From each thing you have let go of
steps.why: Seeing that brings the first practical step: let go of one thing, and that thing can’t hurt you.

steps.quote: hold on to attachment and won’t let go
steps.why: The other side of it: suffering won’t let go of those who won’t let go of attachment.

steps.quote: so that you can let go of attachment
steps.why: Attachment isn’t simply dropped: you hold to the one who has none, in order to let go.

steps.quote: desire, anger and delusion
steps.why: Knowing the truth names what has to go: when even the names of these three are gone, pain is gone.

steps.quote: craving is the seed
steps.why: Then the seed itself: craving is what yields birth without end.

steps.quote: a nature that never changes
steps.why: Craving can never be filled, and the moment you give it up you have a nature that never changes.

threads.title: Fate and effort
threads.note: The book says nothing is stronger than fate. It also says the disgrace is to know what must be known and make no effort, and that those who never falter will see fate’s back. It takes neither back.

steps.quote: What is stronger than fate?
steps.why: Fate stands at full strength here: even as you plan a way around it, it gets there first.

steps.quote: everything that should help can go wrong
steps.why: In making money, what should help can go wrong and what should hurt can turn out well, so the result isn’t yours to command.

steps.quote: The lack of a favouring fate disgraces no one
steps.why: The first turn: lacking a favouring fate is no disgrace, and the disgrace is to know what must be known and make no effort.

steps.quote: effort pays the wages of your body’s toil
steps.why: Even where the result is refused, effort is still paid: the toil earns its wages.

steps.quote: will see the back of fate itself
steps.why: The boldest claim against fate comes last, set beside the first step with neither taken back.

threads.title: From learning to living by it
threads.note: Understanding flows as far as you dig, but hearing isn’t knowing, and knowing isn’t self-control. The thread ends on the book’s plainest demand: live up to what you learned.

steps.quote: gives water as far as you dig
steps.why: Understanding has to be dug for, and it flows only as far as you have dug.

steps.quote: Even if you have no learning, listen.
steps.why: The way stays open to those without books: listening holds you up when you falter.

steps.quote: seeing the reality in it
steps.why: What you take in still has to be tested: whoever says it, understanding means seeing what is real in it.

steps.quote: the conceit that says, “I am wise.”
steps.why: The next danger comes from having got this far: to think “I am wise” is itself immaturity.

steps.quote: still has no self-control
steps.why: Even true knowledge can fail: the greatest fool is someone who understands, teaches, and still has no self-control.

steps.quote: Once you have learned it, live up to it
steps.why: This is what learning is for: once you have it, your life has to match it.

threads.title: How a ruler falls
threads.note: A ruler’s fall starts when he can’t bear to hear bitter words. It ends with the tears of people who can bear no more.

steps.quote: bear words bitter to his ears
steps.why: What keeps a ruler safe is the character to bear words he doesn’t want to hear.

steps.quote: no one to rebuke him
steps.why: Without those words he has no protection, and he can fall with no enemy at all.

steps.quote: isn’t easy to reach
steps.why: Next he closes himself off: hard to reach, looking into nothing, giving no justice.

steps.quote: one who stands with a spear
steps.why: Then power changes what his words are: when he asks, it is a spear saying “Hand it over.”

steps.quote: “Our ruler is harsh”
steps.why: The people begin to say it, and the book counts those bitter words as shortening his days.

steps.quote: The tears wept by those who suffer
steps.why: The weapon that wears away his wealth is the tears of people who suffer and can’t bear it.

threads.title: From weighing to acting
threads.note: First weigh the task, your strength, the time and the place. Then the book turns: weighing must end in a decision, and firmness decides the rest.

steps.quote: Think, then commit to the task.
steps.why: The rule comes first: all the thinking belongs before you commit, none after.

steps.quote: Weigh the strength of the task
steps.why: What to weigh: the task, yourself, the enemy and your allies.

steps.quote: set out on a surge of zeal and broke halfway
steps.why: Zeal can’t stand in for that weighing: many have set out on it and broken halfway.

steps.quote: be like the heron
steps.why: Strength isn’t enough either: there is a time to hold still and a moment to strike.

steps.quote: Ships that run on the sea can’t run on land
steps.why: The place counts too: what rules one ground is useless on another.

steps.quote: The end of deliberation is to reach a decision
steps.why: Here it turns: weighing has an end, and a decision left sitting in delay is a wrong.

steps.quote: Doing it as you said is hard
steps.why: The hard part starts after the words: anyone can say it, few can do it as they said.

steps.quote: if they are firm
steps.why: Everything weighed so far comes down to this: those who plan get what they planned, if they are firm.

threads.title: Where to keep your wealth
threads.note: The book says plainly that wealth counts, and just as plainly that it won’t stay. The one place it says wealth can be stored is the hunger of those who have nothing.

steps.quote: makes people who don’t count into people who do
steps.why: No illusions to begin with: the book says wealth is what makes a person count.

steps.quote: comes by knowing how, and without wrong
steps.why: How it comes matters: wealth made with skill and without wrong gives birth to righteousness and happiness.

steps.quote: It goes the way that crowd goes
steps.why: However well it comes, it goes, as a crowd thins when the dance is over.

steps.quote: do at once the things that stay
steps.why: Since it won’t stay, the question becomes what to do with it now.

steps.quote: have nothing, even with ten million
steps.why: Holding on is no answer: those who neither give nor enjoy have nothing, however much they have.

steps.quote: the village tank filled with water
steps.why: The better way is shown: wealth held for everyone, like a tank the whole village draws on.

steps.quote: That is where someone who has wealth can store it
steps.why: The answer: the place to store wealth is in ending the hunger of those who have nothing.

threads.title: What a friend is for
threads.note: A friend isn’t someone who makes you smile. A friend rebukes you, comes at once in trouble and stays. Ruin shows who that is, and the memory lasts.

steps.quote: makes the heart smile deep within
steps.why: The easy test goes first: a smiling face proves nothing, the heart has to smile.

steps.quote: to step in and rebuke
steps.why: Then it says what friendship is for, and it isn’t laughter: it is stepping in when you go too far.

steps.quote: speak until you weep
steps.why: So that is what to look for: friends who, when you go wrong, can bring you to tears and show you the right way.

steps.quote: takes away trouble on the spot
steps.why: In trouble the same friend moves at once, as a hand catches clothes that slip.

steps.quote: measures your people to their full length
steps.why: Ruin tests all of this: it is the rod that shows you the true length of each of your people.

steps.quote: desert you in your ruin burns the heart
steps.why: Those who fail that test stay with you as a burn, even when death is upon you.

steps.quote: those who wiped away their sorrow
steps.why: The other memory lasts longer still: those who wiped away your sorrow are remembered through seven births.

threads.title: How a habit holds you
threads.note: Liquor and dice hold you the same way: you hide it, reason can’t reach you, a win is the hook, and each loss binds you tighter. The book shows it plainly.

steps.quote: Give up saying, “I have never been drunk.”
steps.why: Denial comes first, and hiding it only makes it show the more.

steps.quote: taking a lamp to look for someone who has dived under water
steps.why: While you are in it, reason can’t reach you: it is a lamp carried to someone under water.

steps.quote: sober for the moment
steps.why: The one opening is the sober moment, when you can see in someone else how you slip.

steps.quote: a hook swallowed by a fish
steps.why: Dice show the same trap from another side: even a win is the hook, not the prize.

steps.quote: destroys your compassion
steps.why: The cost moves inward: first your wealth, then your honesty, then your compassion.

steps.quote: loved more with each loss
steps.why: Why it is so hard to stop: each loss makes it dearer, and the book says the soul is the same with pain.

threads.title: When to bow and when to stand tall
threads.note: Humility adds most to those who have something. It is a strength, and the book gives it a limit: bow in plenty, stand tall when your means shrink.

steps.quote: in the rich it is a further wealth
steps.why: Humility is good in anyone, but it adds most to those who already have something.

steps.quote: Greatness always bends low.
steps.why: Bending becomes the mark of greatness, as admiring yourself is the mark of smallness.

steps.quote: The strength of the capable is bowing.
steps.why: It isn’t weakness: bowing is the weapon the worthy use to turn enemies around.

steps.quote: Accepting defeat, even from those who are not your equals
steps.why: The hardest test of it: to accept defeat from someone who isn’t your equal.

steps.quote: When your means shrink, stand tall.
steps.why: The limit: bowing belongs to plenty, and when you have little the book tells you to stand tall.

threads.title: What poverty does
threads.note: The book doesn’t soften poverty: what it does, what asking costs, and its anger at a world where people must beg. It names no remedy here, though chapter 106 is gentler on asking those fit to give.

steps.quote: Only poverty hurts like poverty.
steps.why: There is no comparing it: nothing else hurts like poverty.

steps.quote: many miseries come and settle
steps.why: It isn’t one pain: many other miseries come to live inside it.

steps.quote: In poverty there is no sleep at all.
steps.why: It won’t let you rest: you could sleep sooner in the middle of a fire.

steps.quote: the life goes out of those who beg
steps.why: Asking costs more still: at a mere word the life goes out of those who beg, and the book turns on those who hide what they have.

steps.quote: let him wander far and perish
steps.why: It ends in anger, not a remedy: if people were meant to live by begging, let the one who made the world perish.

threads.title: From a glance to a flood
threads.note: Desire starts as one look and grows through every joy of union. Then parting comes, and the same desire becomes a flood with no shore.

steps.quote: One look brings sickness
steps.why: Desire starts in her eyes, which hold two looks: one brings the sickness, and the other is its medicine.

steps.quote: the words of the mouth are no use
steps.why: The look is returned, and two people agree before a word is said.

steps.quote: my life puts out new leaves
steps.why: Union comes, and desire feels like life itself growing again at every touch.

steps.quote: Each thing you learn shows up your ignorance
steps.why: It doesn’t settle: each time he holds her he finds how much more there is.

steps.quote: the pain of fearing he will leave
steps.why: Now joy carries a fear inside it: even in union she feels the pain of his leaving.

steps.quote: the pain is greater than that sea
steps.why: Parting comes and she gives the measure: the joy was a sea, and the pain is greater.

steps.quote: swim the fierce flood of desire and see no shore
steps.why: It ends with no comfort: she is swimming, there is no shore, and at midnight she is alone.

threads.title: Trying to forget him
threads.note: He keeps coming into her heart. She asks it for a cure, calls it a fool and resolves to forget him. Then she finds that forgetting costs what remembering costs.

steps.quote: keep coming into mine
steps.why: The memory comes without being asked: he has shut her out of his heart, yet keeps coming into hers.

steps.quote: even remembering burns my heart
steps.why: Her friend tells her to forget, but she asks what would become of her, she doesn’t know how, and even remembering burns.

steps.quote: any cure at all
steps.why: So she turns to her own heart and asks it for a cure.

steps.quote: He has no love for you
steps.why: She tries reason: he has no love for you, so suffering for him is foolish.

steps.quote: you go after the one who left
steps.why: Reason doesn’t hold: the heart still goes after him, and she calls it a fool.

steps.quote: we will lose still more of our beauty
steps.why: She reaches a decision: keep him in your heart and you lose still more of your beauty, so he must be forgotten.

steps.quote: if I forget him today, my beauty will leave me
steps.why: It ends in a bind: told to forget him a little, she answers that forgetting would cost her beauty too.

threads.title: How a sulk comes round
threads.note: The book ends on sulking. A sulk she can’t keep up becomes something both of them want, with its measure and its risk, and the last couplet lands on the embrace that ends it.

steps.quote: my heart forgot that
steps.why: The first sulk can’t even be kept up: her heart forgets it and goes over to him.

steps.quote: the right amount of salt
steps.why: Her friend gives it a measure: a sulk is salt, and drawing it out is a little too much.

steps.quote: a pain even in sulking
steps.why: He feels the risk in it: the sulk may keep them apart too long.

steps.quote: draws out his tenderness
steps.why: She says what it is for: it no longer needs a wrong, because it draws out his tenderness.

steps.quote: it comes back greater
steps.why: The risk turns out to be part of it: his tenderness dims for a moment and comes back greater.

steps.quote: a quarrel is sweeter than making love
steps.why: He reaches the same place from his side: as digesting is sweeter than eating more, so the quarrel beats union.

steps.quote: the embrace that ends it
steps.why: The book’s last couplet lands on the embrace, with its own caution: if you get that far.

chains.title: From effort to righteousness
chains.summary: Effort builds prosperity, and wealth that comes without wrong gives birth to righteousness.

chains.title: What a just ruler sets flowing
chains.summary: The rain is said to depend on the ruler. Farming depends on the rain, and giving depends on those who eat by the work of their own hands.

chains.title: When fate takes wealth away
chains.summary: The fate that takes wealth away brings laziness. Lack of effort lets want in, and poverty brings a weakness from which shameful words are born, even in those of good family.

chains.title: The round of desire
chains.summary: In Part 3 desire feeds on its own quarrels: it needs its sulks, the sulk ends in an embrace, and each embrace shows how much more there is to desire.

chains.title: The way out of rebirth
chains.summary: Wanting truthfulness leads to having no craving, and wanting to want nothing is how you come not to be born.

chains.title: What craving sows
chains.summary: Craving is the seed that yields, for all living things at all times, birth that never ends.

chains.title: Where envy leads
chains.summary: Envy destroys your wealth, and poverty brings a weakness from which shameful words are born.

chains.title: Where gambling leads
chains.summary: Gambling destroys your wealth, and poverty then brings a weakness from which shameful words are born.

chains.title: From a sweet word to compassion
chains.summary: Sweet speech makes righteousness grow, righteousness brings wealth, and compassion thrives with wealth as its foster-mother.

chains.title: From remembered kindness to lasting renown
chains.summary: Recalling one good thing someone did ends even a hurt like killing, and those who bear a wrong have renown until the end.

chains.title: Loving-kindness and what it bears
chains.summary: Loving-kindness makes you warm towards people, and that warmth brings friendship.

chains.title: From listening to a good family name
chains.summary: Humble speech comes hard to those without subtle listening, and a good family name needs that humility.

nodes.label: Chapter 1
nodes.name: கடவுள் வாழ்த்து
nodes.title: Praising God
nodes.summary: A poet praises his own god or the god suited to his subject. He says this is the second: the book treats three goals, each tied to one of the three first gods, so the praise is addressed to all three in common.

nodes.label: Chapter 2
nodes.name: வான்சிறப்பு
nodes.title: The Greatness of Rain
nodes.summary: This chapter tells the greatness of rain, which by god’s command keeps the world going, and with it righteousness, wealth and pleasure. That explains why it follows the praise of god.

nodes.label: Chapter 3
nodes.name: நீத்தார் பெருமை
nodes.title: The Greatness of Those Who Renounce
nodes.summary: This chapter tells the greatness of sages who have renounced completely. They are the ones who show the world righteousness and the rest as they truly are, so it follows the greatness of rain.

nodes.label: Chapter 4
nodes.name: அறன் வலியுறுத்தல்
nodes.title: Insisting on Righteousness
nodes.summary: Of the three those sages teach, righteousness alone, unlike wealth and pleasure, yields this life, the next and release. So this chapter says it is stronger than they are, and that also explains its place.

nodes.label: Chapter 5
nodes.name: இல்வாழ்க்கை
nodes.title: Home Life
nodes.summary: This is the excellence of living with a wife. It follows the chapter on righteousness because it is the first of the two states in which righteousness is done.

nodes.label: Chapter 6
nodes.name: வாழ்க்கைத் துணைநலம்
nodes.title: The Worth of a Wife
nodes.summary: This is the goodness of the wife, the companion of home life. That is why it follows the chapter on home life.

nodes.label: Chapter 7
nodes.name: மக்கட்பேறு
nodes.title: Having Children
nodes.summary: The twice-born owe three debts: to the sages, paid by study, to the gods, paid by sacrifice, and to the ancestors, paid only by begetting sons. This chapter is about having children to pay that debt.

nodes.label: Chapter 8
nodes.name: அன்புடைமை
nodes.title: Loving-kindness
nodes.summary: He defines அன்பு as fondness for your wife, children and others connected to you, and says compassion for all beings grows from it.

nodes.label: Chapter 9
nodes.name: விருந்தோம்பல்
nodes.title: Caring for Guests
nodes.summary: This is caring for guests, expected and unexpected. He ranks it first among household duties, and places it after loving-kindness because only two people joined by loving-kindness can do it.

nodes.label: Chapter 10
nodes.name: இனியவை கூறல்
nodes.title: Speaking Sweet Words
nodes.summary: This means saying sweet words that show the gladness in your mind. Those who care for guests can’t do without it, so it follows that chapter.

nodes.label: Chapter 11
nodes.name: செய்ந்நன்றியறிதல்
nodes.title: Remembering the Good Done to You
nodes.summary: This is not forgetting the good others have done you. It follows sweet speech because, for those who keep household righteousness, the one fault with no escape is destroying a kindness, and this guards against it.

nodes.label: Chapter 12
nodes.name: நடுவு நிலைமை
nodes.title: Standing in the Middle
nodes.summary: This is standing even towards enemies, strangers and friends without slipping from righteousness. It follows the last chapter because remembering a kindness can tempt you to lean towards the one who did it.

nodes.label: Chapter 13
nodes.name: அடக்கம் உடைமை
nodes.title: Restraint
nodes.summary: This is holding body, speech and mind back from evil paths. It follows impartiality because it belongs to someone who sees their own faults as they see a stranger’s.

nodes.label: Chapter 14
nodes.name: ஒழுக்கம் உடைமை
nodes.title: Keeping Good Conduct
nodes.summary: This is keeping the conduct laid down for your varna and stage of life. It follows restraint because only those who have restrained body, speech and mind can do it.

nodes.label: Chapter 15
nodes.name: பிறனில் விழையாமை
nodes.title: Not Wanting Another Man’s Wife
nodes.summary: This is not wanting another man’s wife through the delusion of desire. It follows good conduct because it is found only in those who have good conduct.

nodes.label: Chapter 16
nodes.name: பொறையுடைமை
nodes.title: Bearing Wrongs
nodes.summary: He defines this as bearing it, and not doing the same back, when someone wrongs you for some cause or out of ignorance. It follows the chapter on another’s wife, to say you must bear even with those who leave the path.

nodes.label: Chapter 17
nodes.name: அழுக்காறாமை
nodes.title: Without Envy
nodes.summary: He has already explained envy, at couplet 35. It is the opposite of bearing wrongs, so this chapter, which forbids it, follows that one.

nodes.label: Chapter 18
nodes.name: வெஃகாமை
nodes.title: Without Coveting
nodes.summary: He defines this as not thinking of seizing what belongs to others. It follows the chapter on envy, to say that beyond resenting what others have, even the thought of taking it is a fault.

nodes.label: Chapter 19
nodes.name: புறங்கூறாமை
nodes.title: Without Backbiting
nodes.summary: He defines this as not running people down when they aren’t there. Faults of speech grow from faults of the mind, so it follows the chapters on envy and coveting.

nodes.label: Chapter 20
nodes.name: பயனில சொல்லாமை
nodes.title: No Useless Words
nodes.summary: He defines this as not saying words that bring no righteousness, wealth or pleasure to you or anyone. Householders can’t wholly avoid lies, and harsh words and backbiting are already dealt with, so useless words come next.

nodes.label: Chapter 21
nodes.name: தீவினையச்சம்
nodes.title: Fear of Evil Deeds
nodes.summary: He defines this as being afraid to do what is sin. The chapter gathers up and forbids all the sins of the body, so it follows the chapter on useless words.

nodes.label: Chapter 22
nodes.name: ஒப்புரவறிதல்
nodes.title: Knowing Your Duty to the World
nodes.summary: He defines this as knowing the way of the world and acting on it. The books don’t set it out as they do scriptural conduct: you must know it for yourself. After what to avoid in thought, word and deed, this turns to what remains to be done.

nodes.label: Chapter 23
nodes.name: ஈகை
nodes.title: Giving
nodes.summary: This means giving, without refusing, to the poor who ask. It looks to the next life, so it follows the duty to the world, which looks to this one.

nodes.label: Chapter 24
nodes.name: புகழ்
nodes.title: Renown
nodes.summary: This is the renown that arises in this world and doesn’t die, this life’s reward for those who don’t stray from the household righteousness told so far. It comes mostly from giving, so it follows that chapter.

nodes.label: Chapter 25
nodes.name: அருளுடைமை
nodes.title: Compassion
nodes.summary: He defines compassion as mercy that goes out naturally to all living beings, with no tie behind it. It matters to renunciation as loving-kindness does to household life, so it comes first.

nodes.label: Chapter 26
nodes.name: புலால் மறுத்தல்
nodes.title: Refusing Meat
nodes.summary: He defines this as giving up eating flesh. Eating flesh keeps killing going and also comes from it, so it is both cause and result of that sin. It can’t go with compassion, so this chapter follows that one.

nodes.label: Chapter 27
nodes.name: தவம்
nodes.title: Austerity
nodes.summary: He defines austerity as bearing the pain of vows, such as cutting food and standing in sun, rain and cold so the mind won’t follow the senses, while tending other beings. It comes once refusing meat has ripened compassion.

nodes.label: Chapter 28
nodes.name: கூடா ஒழுக்கம்
nodes.title: Conduct That Doesn’t Fit
nodes.summary: He defines this as evil conduct that doesn’t fit austerity: lacking strength, someone wants again the pleasures of desire they gave up, yet keeps the garb. It follows austerity in order to forbid this.

nodes.label: Chapter 29
nodes.name: கள்ளாமை
nodes.title: Without Stealing
nodes.summary: He defines this as not thinking of taking by deceit anything that belongs to others. For a renouncer the thought is as bad as the act. It deals with faults over wealth, so it follows the chapter on faults of desire.

nodes.label: Chapter 30
nodes.name: வாய்மை
nodes.title: Truthfulness
nodes.summary: வாய்மை is the nature of truth. It forbids lying, which mostly springs from desire and wealth, so it follows the chapters on false conduct and on not stealing.

nodes.label: Chapter 31
nodes.name: வெகுளாமை
nodes.title: Not Getting Angry
nodes.summary: This means not getting angry even when you have cause. It forbids the anger that arises from lying, so it follows the chapter on truthfulness.

nodes.label: Chapter 32
nodes.name: இன்னா செய்யாமை
nodes.title: Doing No Harm
nodes.summary: This means not harming any being, whether for gain, out of hatred or through carelessness. Harm happens without anger too, so it follows the chapter on anger.

nodes.label: Chapter 33
nodes.name: கொல்லாமை
nodes.title: Not Killing
nodes.summary: This means not killing any living thing, from those with five senses to those with one, even by carelessness. It surpasses all the righteousness above and takes in what hasn’t been named, so it comes last.

nodes.label: Chapter 34
nodes.name: நிலையாமை
nodes.title: Impermanence
nodes.summary: Impermanence is the way that nothing that comes to be can last. Those who say what things are differ in many ways, but all accept this. Attachment doesn’t end until it is understood, so it comes first.

nodes.label: Chapter 35
nodes.name: துறவு
nodes.title: Renunciation
nodes.summary: This means letting go of attachment to outer wealth and to the inner body, on seeing that neither lasts. That is also why it follows impermanence.

nodes.label: Chapter 36
nodes.name: மெய்யுணர்தல்
nodes.title: Knowing the Truth
nodes.summary: This means knowing birth, release and their causes as they are, without error or doubt. It too comes from holding to the one who has no attachment, so it follows renunciation.

nodes.label: Chapter 37
nodes.name: அவா அறுத்தல்
nodes.title: Cutting Off Craving
nodes.summary: Those who have cut off deeds past and future still have this body and its fruit, and old habit can draw the mind back to the senses. That thought is a seed of birth, to be cut off by constant knowledge of the truth.

nodes.label: Chapter 38
nodes.name: ஊழ்
nodes.title: Fate
nodes.summary: He treats ஊழ் as the rule that the fruit of your deeds comes back to you, and says wealth and joy both turn on it.

nodes.label: Chapter 39
nodes.name: இறைமாட்சி
nodes.title: The Excellence of a Ruler
nodes.summary: This means the ruler’s good qualities and good deeds. The word இறை is used because he protects the world in the form of the gods who guard it.

nodes.label: Chapter 40
nodes.name: கல்வி
nodes.title: Learning
nodes.summary: This is the ruler learning the right books: on righteousness and statecraft, on elephants, horses, chariots and weapons. It sits among the chapters on rule, but it is spoken generally, because it benefits everyone.

nodes.label: Chapter 41
nodes.name: கல்லாமை
nodes.title: Not Learning
nodes.summary: This means the lowness that comes of not learning. Praising learning wasn’t enough on its own, so it is shown from the other side as well, after the chapter on learning.

nodes.label: Chapter 42
nodes.name: கேள்வி
nodes.title: Listening
nodes.summary: This means hearing the learned explain the meaning of the books. It strengthens the knowledge of those who have learned and gives knowledge to those who haven’t, so it follows the chapters on learning and not learning.

nodes.label: Chapter 43
nodes.name: அறிவுடைமை
nodes.title: Having Understanding
nodes.summary: This means having your own true understanding, alongside what comes from learning and listening.

nodes.label: Chapter 44
nodes.name: குற்றங்கடிதல்
nodes.title: Removing Faults
nodes.summary: This means a ruler keeping six faults out of himself: desire, anger, miserliness, false honour, excess joy and arrogance. Only those with understanding can see and remove them, so it follows that chapter.

nodes.label: Chapter 45
nodes.name: பெரியாரைத் துணைக்கோடல்
nodes.title: Taking the Great as Allies
nodes.summary: A ruler fit to drive the cart of protection takes as helpers men of great wisdom, the ministers and priests who turn him from the bad path to the good and guard him from troubles sent by people or gods.

nodes.label: Chapter 46
nodes.name: சிற்றினம் சேராமை
nodes.title: Keeping Clear of Petty Company
nodes.summary: The petty are those who say good has no good in it and evil no evil, with rakes, libertines and actors. Such a group twists the mind and ruins both worlds, so joining it undoes the help of the great.

nodes.label: Chapter 47
nodes.name: தெரிந்து செயல்வகை
nodes.title: Thinking Before You Act
nodes.summary: How a ruler examines each task before he does it. Once the great have become useful helpers he does this with them, so it follows the chapter on petty company.

nodes.label: Chapter 48
nodes.name: வலியறிதல்
nodes.title: Knowing Your Strength
nodes.summary: A ruler who has settled on punishment among the means measures the four kinds of strength.

nodes.label: Chapter 49
nodes.name: காலமறிதல்
nodes.title: Knowing When to Act
nodes.summary: A ruler with the greater strength, setting out against his enemy, learns the time that suits the march.

nodes.label: Chapter 50
nodes.name: இடனறிதல்
nodes.title: Knowing the Ground
nodes.summary: A ruler who knows his strength and the time, setting out against his enemy, learns the ground on which he can win.

nodes.label: Chapter 51
nodes.name: தெரிந்து தெளிதல்
nodes.title: Testing Before You Trust
nodes.summary: Testing ministers and others by their birth, character, understanding and deeds, then trusting them. A ruler marching on his enemy needs this so that work gets done and no one betrays him.

nodes.label: Chapter 52
nodes.name: தெரிந்து வினையாடல்
nodes.title: Choosing People for the Work
nodes.summary: How a ruler learns which tasks the people he has come to trust can do, and employs them in those tasks.

nodes.label: Chapter 53
nodes.name: சுற்றந் தழால்
nodes.title: Keeping Your Kin Close
nodes.summary: A ruler holds his relatives close so that they don’t leave him. Having spoken of those who do his work, he turns here to the rest of his circle.

nodes.label: Chapter 54
nodes.name: பொச்சாவாமை
nodes.title: Never Growing Careless
nodes.summary: Not growing careless about guarding yourself or destroying your enemies, through delight in your looks, fortune or power. Kin are of use only where there is no such lapse.

nodes.label: Chapter 55
nodes.name: செங்கோன்மை
nodes.title: The Straight Sceptre
nodes.summary: The justice a ruler gives. It leans to neither side, like a straight rod, so it is called the sceptre. Only a ruler free of lapses can give it.

nodes.label: Chapter 56
nodes.name: கொடுங்கோன்மை
nodes.title: The Crooked Sceptre
nodes.summary: The leaning of a ruler’s justice, named again from the rod. It is the opposite of the straight sceptre, so it follows that chapter.

nodes.label: Chapter 57
nodes.name: வெருவந்த செய்யாமை
nodes.title: Not Ruling by Fear
nodes.summary: Not doing what frightens the people, what frightens his officers, or what leaves the ruler himself afraid. Such acts belong with the crooked sceptre, so this chapter follows it.

nodes.label: Chapter 58
nodes.name: கண்ணோட்டம்
nodes.title: Kindly Regard
nodes.summary: This is being unable to refuse what people familiar to you say, once you see them. It happens when your eye goes out to them, hence its name. It expands on what the chapter on not ruling by fear said, so it follows that chapter.

nodes.label: Chapter 59
nodes.name: ஒற்றாடல்
nodes.title: Using Spies
nodes.summary: He says this means employing spies to learn what happens among enemies, neutrals and friends. A ruler needs it both to run his own land and to take others’, so it comes first.

nodes.label: Chapter 60
nodes.name: ஊக்கம் உடைமை
nodes.title: Having Drive
nodes.summary: He defines ஊக்கம் as being roused to act without the mind weakening. Whoever learns through spies what has happened must act on it and needs drive to do so, so this follows the chapter on spies.

nodes.label: Chapter 61
nodes.name: மடி இன்மை
nodes.title: Not Being Lazy
nodes.summary: He defines this as not slacking when you do what you have planned. Even those with drive can at times grow lazy through the pull of their nature, so this follows the chapter on drive.

nodes.label: Chapter 62
nodes.name: ஆள்வினை உடைமை
nodes.title: Persistent Effort
nodes.summary: He defines ஆள்வினை as unbroken, real effort. Getting rid of laziness is not enough, because work is only carried out by effort, so this follows the chapter on laziness.

nodes.label: Chapter 63
nodes.name: இடுக்கண் அழியாமை
nodes.title: Unbroken by Trouble
nodes.summary: He defines this as keeping the mind steady when trouble comes to someone striving at a task, whether it comes from god, from lack of wealth or from the strain on the body.

nodes.label: Chapter 64
nodes.name: அமைச்சு
nodes.title: The Minister
nodes.summary: He defines this as the nature of a minister, meaning his qualities and his actions.

nodes.label: Chapter 65
nodes.name: சொல்வன்மை
nodes.title: Skill in Speech
nodes.summary: He defines this as being able to say the words that carry a minister’s work to the end he intends. It expands “speak with certainty” from K634, so it follows the chapter on the minister.

nodes.label: Chapter 66
nodes.name: வினைத் தூய்மை
nodes.title: Clean Action
nodes.summary: He defines this as work that yields not only wealth but righteousness and fame. Action must be good as well as speech, so this follows the chapter on speech.

nodes.label: Chapter 67
nodes.name: வினைத்திட்பம்
nodes.title: Firmness in Action
nodes.summary: He defines this as the firmness of mind needed by someone who is to carry clean work through to its end.

nodes.label: Chapter 68
nodes.name: வினை செயல்வகை
nodes.title: How to Carry Out Work
nodes.summary: He defines this as the way a minister with such firmness carries out the work.

nodes.label: Chapter 69
nodes.name: தூது
nodes.title: The Envoy
nodes.summary: He defines this as the nature of those sent to other rulers to make peace or war. One kind frames his own words and equals a minister. The other repeats what he was told and has a quarter less of a minister’s qualities.

nodes.label: Chapter 70
nodes.name: மன்னரைச் சேர்ந்து ஒழுகல்
nodes.title: Living Close to Rulers
nodes.summary: He defines this as how ministers should conduct themselves with rulers. “The qualities rulers desire” were asked of the envoy, so this follows that chapter.

nodes.label: Chapter 71
nodes.name: குறிப்பறிதல்
nodes.title: Reading the Unspoken
nodes.summary: He defines this as knowing what a ruler has in mind without being told. It comes here because no one who serves rulers can do without it.

nodes.label: Chapter 72
nodes.name: அவை அறிதல்
nodes.title: Knowing the Assembly
nodes.summary: He defines this as knowing the nature of the assembly around the ruler. When you speak on business you need this as well as reading his mind.

nodes.label: Chapter 73
nodes.name: அவை அஞ்சாமை
nodes.title: Not Fearing the Assembly
nodes.summary: He defines this as having no fear when you speak before an assembly you have judged fit to hear you.

nodes.label: Chapter 74
nodes.name: நாடு
nodes.title: The Country
nodes.summary: This chapter tells of the country, which the ruler and minister carry forward, and which the other parts of the state, such as the fortress, can’t do without.

nodes.label: Chapter 75
nodes.name: அரண்
nodes.title: The Fortress
nodes.summary: The fortress belongs to the country, yet it is named as a part of the state on its own, because when enemies threaten ruin it protects both the country and the ruler.

nodes.label: Chapter 76
nodes.name: பொருள் செயல்வகை
nodes.title: Ways of Making Wealth
nodes.summary: This chapter tells how to make wealth, which is mostly gained through the country and guarded by the fortress.

nodes.label: Chapter 77
nodes.name: படை மாட்சி
nodes.title: The Excellence of an Army
nodes.summary: The army, which wealth provides and which wins victories, takes two chapters. This first one is on what makes an army good.

nodes.label: Chapter 78
nodes.name: படைச் செருக்கு
nodes.title: The Fierce Pride of an Army
nodes.summary: He defines this as an army’s surplus of valour.

nodes.label: Chapter 79
nodes.name: நட்பு
nodes.title: Friendship
nodes.summary: Friendship helps a ruler in his work, as an army does. He gives it five chapters on what to do and twelve on what to avoid, and this is the first of the five.

nodes.label: Chapter 80
nodes.name: நட்பாராய்தல்
nodes.title: Choosing Friends with Care
nodes.summary: You should befriend only those you have examined and found to have the marks given above. This chapter is on how to examine them.

nodes.label: Chapter 81
nodes.name: பழைமை
nodes.title: Old Friendship
nodes.summary: He defines this as bearing the faults of friends because they are old friends. It follows the testing of friends because even tested friends have faults, and fate too makes them err.

nodes.label: Chapter 82
nodes.name: தீ நட்பு
nodes.title: Bad Friendship
nodes.summary: Friendship that must be dropped, because its faults can’t be borne, takes two chapters. This first one is on friendship with people of bad character.

nodes.label: Chapter 83
nodes.name: கூடா நட்பு
nodes.title: Friendship Without the Heart
nodes.summary: He defines this as the friendship of enemies who never join you at heart, but stay close outwardly until they get their chance.

nodes.label: Chapter 84
nodes.name: பேதைமை
nodes.title: Folly
nodes.summary: He turns from friendship to enmity, which springs from anger and desire. Their root is delusion, treated in two chapters, and the first is folly: knowing nothing at all.

nodes.label: Chapter 85
nodes.name: புல்லறிவாண்மை
nodes.title: Petty Understanding
nodes.summary: He turns to the other delusion: to have a small understanding, rate it as great, and refuse the sound words of those above you.

nodes.label: Chapter 86
nodes.name: இகல்
nodes.title: Strife
nodes.summary: Of anger and desire, anger is the greater danger for rulers, so he begins with what anger brings. First comes strife: the discord that makes two sides fight and wear out their strength.

nodes.label: Chapter 87
nodes.name: பகை மாட்சி
nodes.title: Enemies Worth Having
nodes.summary: A ruler can’t be wholly without enemies, so the strife forbidden in general is prescribed here in one special case: enmity made worthwhile because the enemy has faults such as lack of understanding.

nodes.label: Chapter 88
nodes.name: பகைத்திறம் தெரிதல்
nodes.title: Knowing the Ways of Enmity
nodes.summary: He weighs the fault of making unworthy enmity, which enemies to turn into friends or neutrals, what to do with each, how and when to remove the rest, and the harm of failing to.

nodes.label: Chapter 89
nodes.name: உட்பகை
nodes.title: The Enemy Within
nodes.summary: This is the enmity that opens the way for the outer enemy and stays hidden inside until that enemy wins. It too must be removed.

nodes.label: Chapter 90
nodes.name: பெரியாரைப் பிழையாமை
nodes.title: Not Offending the Great
nodes.summary: This is not living in contempt of the great, meaning both rulers, great in power, and sages, great in penance. It closes the chapters on what anger brings.

nodes.label: Chapter 91
nodes.name: பெண்வழிச் சேறல்
nodes.title: Going a Woman’s Way
nodes.summary: What desire brings isn’t enmity outright, but it wrecks gain and brings ruin, so it is counted with enmity. First comes a man following the way of his wife, who should be following his.

nodes.label: Chapter 92
nodes.name: வரைவின் மகளிர்
nodes.title: Women Who Draw No Line
nodes.summary: This is the nature of women who sell their charms to anyone who pays, drawing no line between the fit and the unfit. It follows the faults that come from a man’s own wife.

nodes.label: Chapter 93
nodes.name: கள்ளுண்ணாமை
nodes.title: Not Drinking Liquor
nodes.summary: In ruining conduct and understanding, liquor is like the women of the last chapter. This chapter tells the worth of not drinking it, by speaking of what it does.

nodes.label: Chapter 94
nodes.name: சூது
nodes.title: Gambling
nodes.summary: Like drinking, gambling and illness come between a person and righteousness, wealth and pleasure. This chapter starts on those two with the nature of gambling.

nodes.label: Chapter 95
nodes.name: மருந்து
nodes.title: Medicine
nodes.summary: Diseases come from past deeds and from causes such as unsuitable food and actions. Those from past deeds end only when the deeds are spent, so this chapter sets them aside and tells the medicine for the rest.

nodes.label: Chapter 96
nodes.name: குடிமை
nodes.title: Good Family
nodes.summary: This is the character of those born in a high family. All four varnas can’t do without high birth, so this chapter comes first in its part.

nodes.label: Chapter 97
nodes.name: மானம்
nodes.title: Honour
nodes.summary: He begins the qualities of the well-born with honour: never falling below your standing, and not staying alive when god brings you down. It comes first because it keeps their birth upright.

nodes.label: Chapter 98
nodes.name: பெருமை
nodes.title: Greatness
nodes.summary: Greatness is the nature of the great, shown in doing what is hard, lacking arrogance and not speaking of others’ faults. These arise only where you don’t fall from your standing, so it follows honour.

nodes.label: Chapter 99
nodes.name: சான்றாண்மை
nodes.title: Fullness of Worth
nodes.summary: This is being full of many good qualities and ruling them. It gathers the many qualities that don’t fall under greatness, so it follows that chapter.

nodes.label: Chapter 100
nodes.name: பண்புடைமை
nodes.title: Being Courteous
nodes.summary: This is knowing the nature of everyone and getting along with them, without slipping yourself from greatness and worth. That is why it comes after those chapters.

nodes.label: Chapter 101
nodes.name: நன்றியில் செல்வம்
nodes.title: Wealth That Does No Good
nodes.summary: This is the nature of wealth that is no use to the one who earned it or to anyone else. The owner’s fault is laid on the wealth. The last couplet of the previous chapter pointed here.

nodes.label: Chapter 102
nodes.name: நாணுடைமை
nodes.title: A Sense of Shame
nodes.summary: This is the quality by which those raised high by worth, courtesy and the like feel shame at acts unworthy of them. That is why it follows those chapters.

nodes.label: Chapter 103
nodes.name: குடிசெயல் வகை
nodes.title: Raising Your Family
nodes.summary: This is the art of raising the family you were born into. It belongs to those who feel shame at falling low, so it follows the chapter on shame.

nodes.label: Chapter 104
nodes.name: உழவு
nodes.title: Ploughing
nodes.summary: Ploughing belongs mostly to the cultivators’ varna and a little to merchants, and others may have it done for them. It is the effort that raises a family, so it follows that chapter.

nodes.label: Chapter 105
nodes.name: நல்குரவு
nodes.title: Poverty
nodes.summary: Poverty is having none of the things that can be enjoyed.

nodes.label: Chapter 106
nodes.name: இரவு
nodes.title: Begging
nodes.summary: Begging that leaves your honour whole is as good as not begging, and the books of righteousness say the body, which can reach release, is to be kept even this way. So this chapter forbids the utter renunciation that poverty ended on.

nodes.label: Chapter 107
nodes.name: இரவச்சம்
nodes.title: The Dread of Begging
nodes.summary: This is fear of the begging that costs you your honour.

nodes.label: Chapter 108
nodes.name: கயமை
nodes.title: The Base
nodes.summary: This is the nature of the low, who have none of the qualities the earlier chapters stated or implied. So it comes after all of them.

nodes.label: Chapter 109
nodes.name: தகை அணங்குறுத்தல்
nodes.title: Struck by Her Beauty
nodes.summary: She has left her companions to play in a grove, and he has left his young men to hunt. He comes on her alone, and tells how her beauty torments him. This happens at first sight, so it comes first.

nodes.label: Chapter 110
nodes.name: குறிப்பறிதல்
nodes.title: Reading the Signs
nodes.summary: He says this is the man reading the woman’s signs and her friend’s, and the friend reading both of theirs. The man struck by her beauty needs it if he is to reach her.

nodes.label: Chapter 111
nodes.name: புணர்ச்சி மகிழ்தல்
nodes.title: Delight in Union
nodes.summary: Having read her signs and come together with her, the man speaks of his delight in that union.

nodes.label: Chapter 112
nodes.name: நலம் புனைந்து உரைத்தல்
nodes.title: Praising Her Beauty
nodes.summary: The man dresses her beauty in words of praise. It follows the delight in union, because that is when such praise arises.

nodes.label: Chapter 113
nodes.name: காதற் சிறப்புரைத்தல்
nodes.title: The Greatness of Their Love
nodes.summary: The man and then the woman each say how great their love is. It follows the chapters on union and on her beauty, because such love arises from those.

nodes.label: Chapter 114
nodes.name: நாணுத் துறவுரைத்தல்
nodes.title: Letting Go of Shame
nodes.summary: Turned away and unable to bear it, the man tells her friend he has given up shame. The woman, wanting her love made known, tells her friend the same. This comes when love is at its height.

nodes.label: Chapter 115
nodes.name: அலர் அறிவுறுத்தல்
nodes.title: Telling of the Gossip
nodes.summary: One who wants the secret love to go on tells her friend how the gossip helps. She and her friend, wanting marriage or elopement, tell him of it. It comes once shame has been given up.

nodes.label: Chapter 116
nodes.name: பிரிவு ஆற்றாமை
nodes.title: Unable to Bear Parting
nodes.summary: After marriage he leaves her, for near or far, for righteousness, wealth or joy. This is her inability to bear it, spoken by her friend to him and by her to her friend.

nodes.label: Chapter 117
nodes.name: படர்மெலிந் திரங்கல்
nodes.title: Wasting Away in Grief
nodes.summary: She can’t bear the parting. Thinking always of the pain she suffers, she wastes away and grieves.

nodes.label: Chapter 118
nodes.name: கண் விதுப்பழிதல்
nodes.title: Eyes Aching to See Him
nodes.summary: Her eyes suffer in their haste to see him. This comes after she has wasted away in grief.

nodes.label: Chapter 119
nodes.name: பசப்புறு பருவரல்
nodes.title: The Pain of Pallor
nodes.summary: பசப்பு is the change of colour that comes from being unable to bear parting, and this is the pain of it. It comes when she can’t see him.

nodes.label: Chapter 120
nodes.name: தனிப்படர் மிகுதி
nodes.title: The Grief She Bears Alone
nodes.summary: She says the overflowing grief is hers alone and not his, because he left for righteousness and wealth. It belongs to the woman who has suffered pallor.

nodes.label: Chapter 121
nodes.name: நினைந்தவர் புலம்பல்
nodes.title: The Loneliness of Remembering
nodes.summary: Remembering the joy of their past union, she feels alone, and so does he in his war camp.

nodes.label: Chapter 122
nodes.name: கனவுநிலை உரைத்தல்
nodes.title: Telling the Dream
nodes.summary: She tells her friend about the dream she saw. She dreamed it because she thought of him so much while awake, so this chapter follows the one on lamenting in memory.

nodes.label: Chapter 123
nodes.name: பொழுதுகண்டு இரங்கல்
nodes.title: Grieving at Evening
nodes.summary: When evening comes, she sees it and grieves. She has got through the day on the strength of her dream, so this chapter follows the one on the dream.

nodes.label: Chapter 124
nodes.name: உறுப்புநலன் அழிதல்
nodes.title: Her Beauty Wastes Away
nodes.summary: Her eyes, arms, forehead and other features lose their beauty. This happens when grief is at its height, so the chapter follows the one on grieving at evening.

nodes.label: Chapter 125
nodes.name: நெஞ்சொடு கிளத்தல்
nodes.title: Speaking to Her Heart
nodes.summary: Overwhelmed and with nothing to hold on to, she speaks to her heart, not knowing what to do. This comes once her features have lost their beauty, so it follows that chapter.

nodes.label: Chapter 126
nodes.name: நிறையழிதல்
nodes.title: Reserve Breaks Down
nodes.summary: Overwhelmed by longing, she can’t hold back what she should keep to herself, and lets it out. Reserve means others don’t learn your secrets. It fails because she spoke to her heart, so this chapter follows that one.

nodes.label: Chapter 127
nodes.name: அவர்வயின் விதும்பல்
nodes.title: Longing to Meet
nodes.summary: In a long separation, he and she each hurry with longing to see the other. He rejects the view that this is only her longing for him. Her words here come from lost reserve, so the chapter follows that one.

nodes.label: Chapter 128
nodes.name: குறிப்பறிவுறுத்தல்
nodes.title: Making the Signs Known
nodes.summary: He, she and her friend each make their hidden intent known to one another. This happens once he has come back and they are together, so the chapter follows the one on longing to meet.

nodes.label: Chapter 129
nodes.name: புணர்ச்சி விதும்பல்
nodes.title: Eager for Union
nodes.summary: He and she both hurry towards union. She has made his intent to leave known, yet the eagerness rises in her from her own great longing, so this chapter follows the one on making signs known.

nodes.label: Chapter 130
nodes.name: நெஞ்சொடு புலத்தல்
nodes.title: Sulking with the Heart
nodes.summary: She sulks with her heart, which longs for union and won’t think of sulking even when there is cause, and he does the same with his. That also explains the chapter’s place here.

nodes.label: Chapter 131
nodes.name: புலவி
nodes.title: Sulking
nodes.summary: With neither heart hurrying to union and both meaning to sulk, the two sulk with each other. That also explains the chapter’s place here.

nodes.label: Chapter 132
nodes.name: புலவி நுணுக்கம்
nodes.title: Subtle Sulking
nodes.summary: When he and she are together in bed she has no cause to sulk, but her love runs so high that she imagines a fine cause, lays it on him and sulks. That also explains the chapter’s place here.

nodes.label: Chapter 133
nodes.name: ஊடலுவகை
nodes.title: The Joy of Sulking
nodes.summary: When sulking has made union sweeter, she and he each delight in the sulking.

nodes.label: Kural 1
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: As all letters begin with A, the world begins with the First Lord.

nodes.label: Kural 2
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: What use is learning to those who won’t worship the good feet of the one whose knowledge is pure?

nodes.label: Kural 3
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Those who reach the noble feet of the one who walked on the flower will live long on the earth.

nodes.label: Kural 4
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Those who reach the feet of the one who wants nothing and rejects nothing will have no suffering, ever.

nodes.label: Kural 5
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The two kinds of deeds, which go with darkness, do not touch those devoted to the true praise of the Lord.

nodes.label: Kural 6
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Those who stay on the true path of the one who quenched the five senses will live long.

nodes.label: Kural 7
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Unless you reach the feet of the one who has no equal, the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove.

nodes.label: Kural 8
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Unless you reach the feet of the sage who is a sea of righteousness, the other seas are hard to swim.

nodes.label: Kural 9
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: A head that won’t bow at the feet of the one with eight qualities is as useless as a sense that senses nothing.

nodes.label: Kural 10
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Those who reach the Lord’s feet swim the great sea of births. Those who do not reach them will not.

nodes.label: Kural 11
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Because the rain keeps coming, the world keeps going. So rain should be known as ambrosia.

nodes.label: Kural 12
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Rain makes good food for those who eat, and rain is itself food for them too.

nodes.label: Kural 13
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If the sky fails, hunger will settle in the wide world of spreading waters and torment it.

nodes.label: Kural 14
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If the riches called rain run short, farmers will not plough.

nodes.label: Kural 15
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: It is rain that ruins, and rain again that stands by the ruined and lifts them up. All of it is rain.

nodes.label: Kural 16
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Unless drops fall from the sky, it is hard to see even the head of green grass.

nodes.label: Kural 17
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Even the vast sea would lose its nature, if the clouds took from it and gave nothing back.

nodes.label: Kural 18
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If the sky dries up, festivals and worship will cease here, even for the gods.

nodes.label: Kural 19
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If the sky does not give, neither giving nor austerity will remain in the wide world.

nodes.label: Kural 20
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If the world can’t go on without water, then for everyone, conduct can’t go on without rain.

nodes.label: Kural 21
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The settled view of the books is that the greatness of those who renounce while holding to right conduct stands above all else.

nodes.label: Kural 22
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Trying to measure the greatness of those who renounce is like counting all who have died on earth.

nodes.label: Kural 23
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The greatness of those who have weighed the two and taken up righteousness here shines out in the world.

nodes.label: Kural 24
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Whoever guards the five senses with the goad called firmness is a seed for the land called the highest.

nodes.label: Kural 25
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Of the strength of one who quenched the five senses, Indra himself, ruler of those in the wide sky, is witness enough.

nodes.label: Kural 26
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Those who do what is hard to do are great. Those who can’t are small.

nodes.label: Kural 27
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The world lies with the one who knows the workings of the five: taste, light, touch, sound and smell.

nodes.label: Kural 28
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The hidden words of people whose speech comes true show their greatness on earth.

nodes.label: Kural 29
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The anger of those who stand on the hill called virtue is hard to withstand, even for a moment.

nodes.label: Kural 30
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Those called sages are the righteous, because they live with tenderness towards every living thing.

nodes.label: Kural 31
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Righteousness brings distinction and it brings wealth. What gain could be greater for a living being?

nodes.label: Kural 32
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: There is no gain greater than righteousness, and no ruin greater than forgetting it.

nodes.label: Kural 33
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: However you can, never stopping, do righteous deeds everywhere they can be done.

nodes.label: Kural 34
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: To be without stain in your mind is all of righteousness. Everything else is noise.

nodes.label: Kural 35
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Envy, craving, anger and harsh words: righteousness is a life free of these four.

nodes.label: Kural 36
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Don’t say “I’ll see to it some other day.” Practise righteousness, for it is the companion that doesn’t die when you die.

nodes.label: Kural 37
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: You needn’t be told what the way of righteousness is. See it between the one who bears the palanquin and the one who rides in it.

nodes.label: Kural 38
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If you do good and let no day fall away, that is a stone that blocks the road of your living days.

nodes.label: Kural 39
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Only what comes from righteousness is joy. All else is outside it, and brings no praise.

nodes.label: Kural 40
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: What you ought to do is righteousness. What you ought to avoid is whatever brings blame.

nodes.label: Kural 41
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The one called a householder is a steady support on the good path for the three who live as they should.

nodes.label: Kural 42
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The one called a householder is the support of those who have renounced, those who have nothing, and the dead.

nodes.label: Kural 43
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The ancestors in the south, the gods, guests, kin and yourself: looking after these five is the chief duty.

nodes.label: Kural 44
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If your life fears blame and shares its food, your line will never die out.

nodes.label: Kural 45
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If home life has loving-kindness and righteousness, that is its quality and its fruit.

nodes.label: Kural 46
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If you live your home life in the way of righteousness, what would you gain by going off on some outside path?

nodes.label: Kural 47
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The one who lives home life as it should be lived is first among all who strive.

nodes.label: Kural 48
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: A home life that keeps others on their path and doesn’t slip from righteousness has more endurance than those who do penance.

nodes.label: Kural 49
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: What is called righteousness is home life, and it too is good if no one else can blame it.

nodes.label: Kural 50
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: One who lives in this world as a life should be lived will be counted among the gods who dwell in the sky.

nodes.label: Kural 51
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: She is a life’s companion who has the worth a home needs and lives within the means of the man who took her.

nodes.label: Kural 52
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If a wife lacks the worth a home needs, that life is nothing, however fine it may be.

nodes.label: Kural 53
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: What is lacking if the wife has worth? What is there if she has none?

nodes.label: Kural 54
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: What is greater than a woman, if she has the strength called chastity?

nodes.label: Kural 55
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: A woman who worships no god but wakes worshipping her husband has only to say “Rain”, and it rains.

nodes.label: Kural 56
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: A woman is one who guards herself, cares for the man who took her, guards their good name and never flags.

nodes.label: Kural 57
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: What use is guarding women behind walls? The best guard is the one they keep by their own restraint.

nodes.label: Kural 58
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If women gain the man who gained them, they gain great honour in the world where the gods live.

nodes.label: Kural 59
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Those without a wife who cares for a good name can’t walk proud as a bull before those who scorn them.

nodes.label: Kural 60
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: They call the excellence of a home a blessing, and having good children its fine ornament.

nodes.label: Kural 61
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Of all that can be gained, we know of nothing else like children with understanding.

nodes.label: Kural 62
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: In all seven births, evils won’t touch you if you have children of good character, free of blame.

nodes.label: Kural 63
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: People say their children are their wealth. That wealth comes by each one’s own deeds.

nodes.label: Kural 64
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Sweeter by far than ambrosia is the porridge your own children have stirred with their small hands.

nodes.label: Kural 65
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Touching your children’s bodies is joy to the body, and hearing their words is joy to the ear.

nodes.label: Kural 66
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: “The flute is sweet, the harp is sweet,” say those who have not heard the babble of their own children.

nodes.label: Kural 67
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The good a father does his son is to put him in the front rank of the assembly.

nodes.label: Kural 68
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: That your children know more than you is sweet to every living being on this great earth.

nodes.label: Kural 69
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: A mother who hears her son called a man of worth feels more joy than when she bore him.

nodes.label: Kural 70
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: What a son does in return for his father is to make people say, “What penance did his father do to have him?”

nodes.label: Kural 71
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Can any lock keep loving-kindness hidden? The tears of those who have it will give it away.

nodes.label: Kural 72
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: People without loving-kindness keep everything for themselves. People with it would give even their bones for others.

nodes.label: Kural 73
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: They say the precious soul is joined to a body of bone so that it can practise loving-kindness.

nodes.label: Kural 74
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Loving-kindness makes you warm towards people, and that warmth brings friendship, a gift beyond measure.

nodes.label: Kural 75
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: They say the happiness of those who are happy in this world comes from a life settled in loving-kindness.

nodes.label: Kural 76
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Only the ignorant say loving-kindness helps righteousness alone. It helps against hostility too.

nodes.label: Kural 77
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: As the sun scorches a creature with no bones, righteousness scorches a person with no loving-kindness.

nodes.label: Kural 78
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: A life with no loving-kindness inside is like a dead tree trying to sprout on barren ground.

nodes.label: Kural 79
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: What use is everything on the outside to someone who lacks loving-kindness, the part within?

nodes.label: Kural 80
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: A living body is one that loving-kindness moves. Without it, a body is just bones wrapped in skin.

nodes.label: Kural 81
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The whole point of staying at home and keeping things up is to care for guests and do them good.

nodes.label: Kural 82
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: To eat while your guest stays outside is not to be wished for, even if it is the medicine against death.

nodes.label: Kural 83
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The life of one who cares for the guests who come each day will not suffer and fall to ruin.

nodes.label: Kural 84
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: With a glad heart the goddess of fortune lives in the home of one who cares for good guests with a glad face.

nodes.label: Kural 85
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Need you even sow seed in the field of one who feeds guests and eats what is left?

nodes.label: Kural 86
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: One who looks after the guest who is leaving and watches for the guest still to come is a good guest to those in the sky.

nodes.label: Kural 87
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: There is no saying how great the fruit of the sacrifice is. It is measured by the worth of the guest.

nodes.label: Kural 88
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: After anxious guarding they will say “We have nothing to hold on to”: those who never took up the sacrifice of caring for guests.

nodes.label: Kural 89
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Poverty amid plenty is the folly of neglecting guests. It is found among fools.

nodes.label: Kural 90
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The aṉiccam flower wilts when you smell it. A guest wilts when you look at them with a changed face.

nodes.label: Kural 91
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Sweet words are what come from the mouths of those who have seen the truth: steeped in tenderness and free of deceit.

nodes.label: Kural 92
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Better than giving with a glad heart is to have a glad face and sweet words.

nodes.label: Kural 93
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Righteousness lies in a glad face, a kind look and sweet words that come from the heart.

nodes.label: Kural 94
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The poverty that brings sorrow will not come to those whose sweet words bring joy to everyone.

nodes.label: Kural 95
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Humility and sweet words are a person’s ornaments. Nothing else is.

nodes.label: Kural 96
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If you seek out what is good and say it sweetly, wrongs will wear away and righteousness will grow.

nodes.label: Kural 97
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Words that are useful and never part from courtesy give rise to fairness and bring good.

nodes.label: Kural 98
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Sweet words free of all meanness bring joy in the next life and in this one.

nodes.label: Kural 99
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If you have seen what joy sweet words bring, why use hard words?

nodes.label: Kural 100
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: To speak harsh words when sweet ones are there is like picking unripe fruit when ripe fruit is there.

nodes.label: Kural 101
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: For help you did nothing to earn, even earth and sky are hardly a fair return.

nodes.label: Kural 102
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: A good deed done at the right time, though small, is far greater than the world.

nodes.label: Kural 103
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Weigh the goodness of help given with no thought of return, and it is greater than the sea.

nodes.label: Kural 104
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Though the good done them is the size of a millet seed, those who know its worth take it as the size of a palmyra.

nodes.label: Kural 105
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The measure of help is not the help itself. It is the worth of those who received it.

nodes.label: Kural 106
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Don’t forget the bond of the stainless. Don’t give up the friendship of those who stood by you in trouble.

nodes.label: Kural 107
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Through seven lives and seven births, people remember the friendship of those who wiped away their sorrow.

nodes.label: Kural 108
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: It is not good to forget a good deed. It is good to forget what is not good, that very day.

nodes.label: Kural 109
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Though someone hurts you as if they were killing you, it all dies when you recall one good thing they did.

nodes.label: Kural 110
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Those who have killed any good may still escape. There is no escape for the man who killed the good done to him.

nodes.label: Kural 111
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: What is called fairness is good, if you can give each side its due.

nodes.label: Kural 112
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The gains of one who is upright don’t fall apart, and are a strength to those who come after.

nodes.label: Kural 113
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Even if it brings only good, let go at once of gain that comes from leaving the middle.

nodes.label: Kural 114
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Whether people are worthy or unworthy is seen by what each leaves behind.

nodes.label: Kural 115
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Loss and gain will always come. A heart that doesn’t lean is the ornament of the worthy.

nodes.label: Kural 116
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If your heart leaves the middle and does wrong, know this: “I will be ruined.”

nodes.label: Kural 117
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The world does not count it ruin when someone who stays in the middle and in the good falls low.

nodes.label: Kural 118
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: To be like the balance that rests level and then weighs true, leaning to neither side, is the ornament of the worthy.

nodes.label: Kural 119
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Uprightness is speech that does not bend, if you have made sure there is no bend within.

nodes.label: Kural 120
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: For traders, good trade is to care for others’ goods as their own.

nodes.label: Kural 121
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Restraint will carry you among the immortals. Lack of restraint will drive you into deep darkness.

nodes.label: Kural 122
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Guard restraint as wealth. There is no greater gain for a life.

nodes.label: Kural 123
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If you know what is worth knowing and hold yourself in by the right way, your restraint will be noticed and bring you honour.

nodes.label: Kural 124
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: One who holds steady in their place and keeps restraint stands taller than a mountain.

nodes.label: Kural 125
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Humility is good in everyone, but in the rich it is a further wealth.

nodes.label: Kural 126
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If in one life you can draw in the five senses as a tortoise draws in its limbs, it will shelter you through seven lives.

nodes.label: Kural 127
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Whatever else you fail to guard, guard your tongue. If you don’t, you will suffer from the slips of your speech.

nodes.label: Kural 128
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: If a single evil word does its harm, the good you have done turns bad.

nodes.label: Kural 129
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: A wound burned by fire heals within. A scar burned by the tongue never heals.

nodes.label: Kural 130
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Righteousness finds the path to someone who holds back anger, learns and keeps restraint, and waits for the moment to see them.

nodes.label: Kural 131
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Conduct brings excellence, so guard your conduct more closely than your life.

nodes.label: Kural 132
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Guard your conduct with anxious care. Search and test as you will, it alone is your companion.

nodes.label: Kural 133
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Good conduct is noble family. A lapse in it becomes low birth.

nodes.label: Kural 134
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: A Brahmin who forgets his scripture can learn it again. If his conduct falls, his birth is ruined.

nodes.label: Kural 135
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Just as the envious have no gain, those without good conduct have no standing.

nodes.label: Kural 136
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The strong-minded don’t slacken in their conduct, for they know the harm that comes of a lapse.

nodes.label: Kural 137
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: By good conduct people reach greatness. By a lapse they reach blame they didn’t deserve.

nodes.label: Kural 138
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Good conduct is the seed of good. Bad conduct brings suffering always.

nodes.label: Kural 139
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Those with good conduct can’t say evil things with their mouths, even by a slip.

nodes.label: Kural 140
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Those who don’t learn to move in step with the world may learn much, but they are still without understanding.

nodes.label: Kural 141
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The folly of chasing a woman who is another man’s property is not found in those who know righteousness and wealth.

nodes.label: Kural 142
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Of all who stand outside righteousness, none is a greater fool than those who stand at another man’s door.

nodes.label: Kural 143
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Those who do evil in the home of someone who trusts them are surely no different from the dead.

nodes.label: Kural 144
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: However great you may be, what good is it, if you enter another man’s home without a millet seed’s worth of thought?

nodes.label: Kural 145
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Whoever trespasses on a home, thinking it easy, earns blame that will never die.

nodes.label: Kural 146
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Enmity, sin, fear and blame: these four never leave the one who trespasses on a home.

nodes.label: Kural 147
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The one who doesn’t crave the womanhood of a woman who is another’s is the one called a householder who lives by righteousness.

nodes.label: Kural 148
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The great manhood that won’t look at another’s wife is, for the worthy, not only righteousness but full conduct.

nodes.label: Kural 149
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Who in this world ringed by the fearsome sea deserves every good? Those who don’t embrace the shoulders of a woman who is another’s.

nodes.label: Kural 150
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Even if you keep no bounds of righteousness and do wrong, it is good not to crave the womanhood of one within another’s bounds.

nodes.label: Kural 151
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: As the earth holds up those who dig into it, the highest thing is to bear with those who scorn you.

nodes.label: Kural 152
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: Always bear a wrong done to you. Forgetting it is better still.

nodes.label: Kural 153
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
nodes.snippet: The deepest poverty is to turn a guest away. The greatest strength is to bear with fools.

nodes.label: Kural 154
nodes.speaker: tiruvalluvar
