nodes.label: Kural 1145
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: As getting drunk makes you want more toddy, so desire is sweeter each time it comes out in the open.

nodes.label: Kural 1146
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: We saw each other just one day, yet the gossip is like the snake seizing the moon.

nodes.label: Kural 1147
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: The town’s gossip is the manure and my mother’s words the water, and this sickness grows on.

nodes.label: Kural 1148
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: To say you will put out desire with gossip is like saying you will put out a fire with ghee.

nodes.label: Kural 1149
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: He told me not to be afraid, and then left me, to the shame of many. Can I still be ashamed of gossip?

nodes.label: Kural 1150
nodes.speaker: friend
nodes.snippet: This town is raising the gossip we wanted. If he wishes, your lover will be kind.

nodes.label: Kural 1151
nodes.speaker: friend
nodes.snippet: If you aren’t going, tell me. If it is your quick return, tell that to whoever will still be alive.

nodes.label: Kural 1152
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Even a look from him used to be sweet. Now our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave.

nodes.label: Kural 1153
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: It is hard to trust. Even those who understand can sometimes leave.

nodes.label: Kural 1154
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: If the one who was tender and said “Don’t be afraid” goes away, is there any fault in those who trusted what he swore?

nodes.label: Kural 1155
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: If you would save me, stop the one who is mine from leaving. If he goes, it will be hard to meet again.

nodes.label: Kural 1156
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: If he is hard enough to tell me he’s leaving, there is little hope that he will be kind.

nodes.label: Kural 1157
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Won’t these bangles slipping from my forearm spread the word that the lord of the shore has left me?

nodes.label: Kural 1158
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: It is painful to live in a town without your own people. More painful still is parting from those dear to you.

nodes.label: Kural 1159
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Fire burns if you touch it. Can it burn when you leave it, as the sickness of desire does?

nodes.label: Kural 1160
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Many do the hard thing, drive off the sickness of grief, bear the parting and go on living afterwards.

nodes.label: Kural 1161
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: I would hide this sickness, but it rises like spring water for those who draw it.

nodes.label: Kural 1162
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: I can’t hide this sickness, and telling the one who caused it brings me shame.

nodes.label: Kural 1163
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Desire and shame hang from my life as from a carrying pole, inside this body that can’t bear them.

nodes.label: Kural 1164
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: There is indeed a sea of desire. There is no safe raft to cross it.

nodes.label: Kural 1165
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Those who can bring suffering even in friendship, what would they do in enmity?

nodes.label: Kural 1166
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: The joy of desire is a sea. But when it turns on you, the pain is greater than that sea.

nodes.label: Kural 1167
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: I swim the fierce flood of desire and see no shore. Even at midnight I alone am here.

nodes.label: Kural 1168
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Poor night. It has put all living things to sleep and has no companion but me.

nodes.label: Kural 1169
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Crueller even than that cruel one’s cruelty are these nights that now drag on.

nodes.label: Kural 1170
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: If my eyes could go where he is, as my heart does, they wouldn’t be swimming in this flood of water.

nodes.label: Kural 1171
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Why do my eyes weep now? It was through their showing that I came to see this endless sickness.

nodes.label: Kural 1172
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: These kohl-lined eyes looked without knowing what would come. Why do they now suffer, not understanding?

nodes.label: Kural 1173
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: My eyes rushed to look, and now they weep by themselves. There is something laughable in this.

nodes.label: Kural 1174
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: My kohl-lined eyes have left in me a sickness I can’t escape or survive, and now they can’t weep, their water gone.

nodes.label: Kural 1175
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: My eyes, which gave me a sickness of desire too great for the sea, now suffer and can’t close.

nodes.label: Kural 1176
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Oh, how sweet! The eyes that gave me this sickness have fallen into it themselves.

nodes.label: Kural 1177
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Let them suffer and suffer till their water runs out, these eyes that longed and longed and begged to see him.

nodes.label: Kural 1178
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: There is one who wanted me without cherishing me. Still, my eyes will not rest until they see him.

nodes.label: Kural 1179
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: When he doesn’t come they don’t sleep. When he comes they don’t sleep. Either way my eyes are in deep pain.

nodes.label: Kural 1180
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: It isn’t hard for the town to find out the secret of those like me, whose eyes are beaten drums.

nodes.label: Kural 1181
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: I agreed to go without the kindness of the one who loved me. Who can I tell now that I have turned pale?

nodes.label: Kural 1182
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Proud to say “He gave me,” pallor climbs on my body and rides it.

nodes.label: Kural 1183
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: He took my beauty and my shame, and in exchange gave me sickness and pallor.

nodes.label: Kural 1184
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: I think of him, and what I talk of is his worth. So is this pallor a fraud?

nodes.label: Kural 1185
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Look there, my lover going away. Look here, pallor spreading over my body.

nodes.label: Kural 1186
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: As darkness waits for a lamp to fail, pallor waits for my husband’s embrace to slacken.

nodes.label: Kural 1187
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: I lay holding him and shifted a little. That was enough: pallor came on so thick you could scoop it up.

nodes.label: Kural 1188
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: People say, “She has turned pale.” No one says, “He has left her.”

nodes.label: Kural 1189
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Let my body turn as pale as it will, if the one who talked me into this is then in the right.

nodes.label: Kural 1190
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: It is well to be called pallor itself, if people don’t spread it about that the one who won me is unkind.

nodes.label: Kural 1191
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Those whose love is returned by the one they love have found the stoneless fruit of desire.

nodes.label: Kural 1192
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: The kindness of lovers to those who love them is like rain from the sky to those who live by it.

nodes.label: Kural 1193
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Only those loved by the ones they love can have the pride of saying, “We will live.”

nodes.label: Kural 1194
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Even those who are held dear are without blessing, if the one they love doesn’t love them back.

nodes.label: Kural 1195
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: What can the one I love do for me, if he doesn’t love me too?

nodes.label: Kural 1196
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Desire on one side only is painful. Like the load on a carrying pole, it is sweet when it is on both sides.

nodes.label: Kural 1197
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: The god of desire stays on one side only. Doesn’t he see my pain and my grief?

nodes.label: Kural 1198
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: No one in the world is as hard as those who go on living without a sweet word from the one they love.

nodes.label: Kural 1199
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Even if the one I long for isn’t kind to me, any word of him is sweet to my ears.

nodes.label: Kural 1200
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Long may you live, my heart. You would tell your sickness to one who isn’t close to you. Fill in the sea instead.

nodes.label: Kural 1201
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Desire is sweeter than toddy, because even thinking of it brings a great joy that doesn’t fade.

nodes.label: Kural 1202
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Desire is sweet in every way. When you think of the one you love, no pain comes.

nodes.label: Kural 1203
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: A sneeze starts to come and then dies away. Does he seem about to think of me, and then not?

nodes.label: Kural 1204
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Am I too in his heart? In mine, oh, he is always there.

nodes.label: Kural 1205
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: He has barred me from his heart. Isn’t he ashamed to keep coming into mine?

nodes.label: Kural 1206
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: How else would I live? I live by remembering the days I was with him.

nodes.label: Kural 1207
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: What would become of me if I forgot? I don’t know how to forget, and even remembering burns my heart.

nodes.label: Kural 1208
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: However much I think of him, he doesn’t get angry. Isn’t that the honour my lover does me?

nodes.label: Kural 1209
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: My sweet life is ending, as I dwell on the unkindness of the one who said, “We are not separate.”

nodes.label: Kural 1210
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Long may you live, moon. Don’t set, so that my eyes may see the one who left without leaving me.

nodes.label: Kural 1211
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: What feast can I give the dream that came with a message from my lover?

nodes.label: Kural 1212
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: If my eyes, carp-shaped and dark with kohl, would sleep when I beg them, I could tell the one who held me that I have survived.

nodes.label: Kural 1213
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: He shows me no kindness when I am awake, but I see him in dreams, and that is what keeps me alive.

nodes.label: Kural 1214
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: In dreams I have the joy of desire, because a dream seeks out the man who shows no kindness when I am awake and brings him to me.

nodes.label: Kural 1215
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Even seeing him awake was sweet only at that moment. The dream too is sweet only while I am seeing it.

nodes.label: Kural 1216
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: If there were no such thing as waking, my lover would never leave me in my dreams.

nodes.label: Kural 1217
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: He is cruel, giving me no kindness when I am awake. Why does he torment me in my dreams?

nodes.label: Kural 1218
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: When I sleep, he is on my shoulders. When I wake, he rushes into my heart.

nodes.label: Kural 1219
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Those who never see a lover in their dreams blame him for showing no kindness in waking life.

nodes.label: Kural 1220
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: They say he left me in waking life. Do the people of this village not see him in their dreams?

nodes.label: Kural 1221
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Long may you live, hour. You are no evening, but the time that eats the lives of those who have wed.

nodes.label: Kural 1222
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: You are wretched, dim evening, long may you live. Is your mate as hard-hearted as mine?

nodes.label: Kural 1223
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Evening comes with cold budding and its light growing pale, and with it despair buds in me and pain grows.

nodes.label: Kural 1224
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: When my lover is away, evening comes like strangers to a killing ground.

nodes.label: Kural 1225
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: What good did I do the morning, and what harm did I do the evening?

nodes.label: Kural 1226
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Before the one who wed me left, I never knew that evening brings pain.

nodes.label: Kural 1227
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: This sickness buds in the morning, fills out all day and flowers in the evening.

nodes.label: Kural 1228
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: The cowherd’s flute is a messenger for the evening that burns like fire, and a weapon that kills.

nodes.label: Kural 1229
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: When evening spreads and reason reels, the town reels too, and suffers.

nodes.label: Kural 1230
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: My life has not died yet, but in this dim evening it is dying, as I think of the man whose way is wealth.

nodes.label: Kural 1231
nodes.speaker: friend
nodes.snippet: He went far away and left us this misery. As you think of him, your eyes now shrink in shame before sweet flowers.

nodes.label: Kural 1232
nodes.speaker: friend
nodes.snippet: Your eyes, pale and streaming with tears, seem to be telling of the unkindness of the one you long for.

nodes.label: Kural 1233
nodes.speaker: friend
nodes.snippet: Your arms, which swelled on the day he wed you, seem to be proclaiming that he has gone.

nodes.label: Kural 1234
nodes.speaker: friend
nodes.snippet: With your companion gone, your arms have lost their old beauty. Now they shrink and the gold bangles slip away.

nodes.label: Kural 1235
nodes.speaker: friend
nodes.snippet: Your arms, their bangles gone and their old beauty withered, tell of the cruelty of a cruel man.

nodes.label: Kural 1236
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: My arms grow thin and my bangles slip, and I ache to hear him called cruel.

nodes.label: Kural 1237
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Will you win glory, my heart, by telling that cruel man about the uproar over my wasting arms?

nodes.label: Kural 1238
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: When I loosened my arms in our embrace, the forehead of that simple girl in gold bangles turned pale.

nodes.label: Kural 1239
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: When a cool breeze cut through our embrace, the simple girl’s great rain-cool eyes turned pale.

nodes.label: Kural 1240
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Even the pallor in her eyes suffered when it saw what her bright forehead had done.

nodes.label: Kural 1241
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Won’t you think of something, heart, and tell me any cure at all for this unending sickness?

nodes.label: Kural 1242
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: He has no love for you, yet you go on suffering. That is foolishness, my heart, long may you live.

nodes.label: Kural 1243
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Why sit here thinking of him and aching, heart? The one who gave us this sickness of grief has no tender thought for us.

nodes.label: Kural 1244
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Take my eyes with you too when you go, heart. Wanting to see him, they are eating me.

nodes.label: Kural 1245
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: We are drawn to him and he isn’t drawn to us. Can we give him up as an enemy, heart?

nodes.label: Kural 1246
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: When you see the lover who mends a sulk with an embrace, you can’t even sulk. Your anger now is a pretence, my heart.

nodes.label: Kural 1247
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Good heart, give up desire or give up modesty. I can’t bear them both.

nodes.label: Kural 1248
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: You pine because he won’t show tender kindness, and you go after the one who left. You are a fool, my heart.

nodes.label: Kural 1249
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Your lover is within you, my heart. Whom are you thinking of, and to whom are you going?

nodes.label: Kural 1250
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: If we keep in our heart the one who left us and won’t come near, we will lose still more of our beauty.

nodes.label: Kural 1251
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: The axe of desire breaks down the door of reserve, bolted with modesty.

nodes.label: Kural 1252
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: This thing called desire has no mercy. Even in the dead of night it rules my heart and puts it to work.

nodes.label: Kural 1253
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: I would hide my desire, but it comes out without warning, like a sneeze.

nodes.label: Kural 1254
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: I used to say I had reserve. Now my desire has gone past hiding, out into the public square.

nodes.label: Kural 1255
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: The great dignity of not going after those who hurt you is not something known to people with the sickness of desire.

nodes.label: Kural 1256
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: It makes me want to go after the one who hurt me. What a fine thing, this sorrow that has come to me!

nodes.label: Kural 1257
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: When the one we cherish does, in desire, all we long for, we don’t even know there is such a thing as modesty.

nodes.label: Kural 1258
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Aren’t the humble words of that thief of many tricks the army that breaks down our womanhood?

nodes.label: Kural 1259
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: I went off meaning to sulk. I saw my heart was ready to join him, and I embraced him.

nodes.label: Kural 1260
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Can those whose hearts are like fat in a fire say, when they come together, that they will hold to their sulk?

nodes.label: Kural 1261
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: My eyes have lost their light and grown dull, and my fingers have worn down from touching off the days since he left.

nodes.label: Kural 1262
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: You in your bright jewels, if I forget him today, my beauty will leave me and the bangles will slip from my arms.

nodes.label: Kural 1263
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: He left wanting victory, with his will for his companion. Wanting his return, I am still alive.

nodes.label: Kural 1264
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Thinking of the return of the one who left, with all the desire we shared, my heart grows branches and climbs.

nodes.label: Kural 1265
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Let me see my husband until my eyes are full. Once I have, the pallor will leave my soft shoulders.

nodes.label: Kural 1266
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Let my husband come, just one day. I will drink until all this sickness of grief is gone.

nodes.label: Kural 1267
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: When the one as dear as my eyes comes, shall I sulk, shall I embrace him, or shall I join with him?

nodes.label: Kural 1268
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: May the ruler throw himself into the work and win. Then I will go to my wife and give the evening a feast.

nodes.label: Kural 1269
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: For those who pine, counting on the day when the one far away returns, one day passes like seven.

nodes.label: Kural 1270
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Once her heart has broken and spilled, what use is it if she will have me, if she has me, if she holds me?

nodes.label: Kural 1271
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Though you hide it, your kohl-dark eyes slip your control and refuse. There is something they want to say.

nodes.label: Kural 1272
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: This simple girl, with beauty that fills my eyes and arms like bamboo, has a woman’s nature in great measure.

nodes.label: Kural 1273
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Like the thread that shows through a bead, something shows through this young woman’s adornment.

nodes.label: Kural 1274
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: As fragrance lies inside a closed bud, something lies inside the budding smile of this simple girl.

nodes.label: Kural 1275
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: The stealth of the woman in close-set bangles, done and gone past me, holds a medicine for the great pain I feel.

nodes.label: Kural 1276
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: He comforts me so fully and joins me so gladly, but in it I see myself bearing pain again and thinking he has no love.

nodes.label: Kural 1277
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: My bangles knew before we did that the man of the cool shore had drawn away.

nodes.label: Kural 1278
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: It was only yesterday my lover left, and I have been pale in body for seven days.

nodes.label: Kural 1279
nodes.speaker: friend
nodes.snippet: She looked at her bangles, looked at her soft arms, looked at her feet. That is what she did there.

nodes.label: Kural 1280
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: To tell the sickness of desire with the eyes and beg: they say this is womanhood on top of womanhood.

nodes.label: Kural 1281
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: To be drunk at a thought and elated at a glance: toddy can’t do this, but desire can.

nodes.label: Kural 1282
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: When desire comes full, as tall as a palmyra, you must not sulk even by a millet seed.

nodes.label: Kural 1283
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Though he shows me no regard and does just as he likes, my eyes can’t rest without seeing my husband.

nodes.label: Kural 1284
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: I went there to sulk, my friend, but my heart forgot that and went to join him.

nodes.label: Kural 1285
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Like the eye that can’t see the stick painting it with kohl, I can’t see my husband’s faults when I see him.

nodes.label: Kural 1286
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: When I see him I see no faults. When I don’t see him I see nothing but faults.

nodes.label: Kural 1287
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Like people who jump into a flood knowing it will sweep them away, what use is it to sulk, knowing it will fail?

nodes.label: Kural 1288
nodes.speaker: friend
nodes.snippet: Your chest, you thief, is like toddy to those drunk on it. However shameful the harm it does, they want more.

nodes.label: Kural 1289
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Desire is softer than a flower. Few ever find it at its peak.

nodes.label: Kural 1290
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: She sulked with her eyes alone, then gave way, more eager to embrace than I was.

nodes.label: Kural 1291
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: You see how his heart stands by him. Why, heart, won’t you stand by me?

nodes.label: Kural 1292
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Even when you see he isn’t drawn to us, my heart, you go to him, sure he won’t be angry.

nodes.label: Kural 1293
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Is it because the ruined have no friends, heart, that you go after him as you please?

nodes.label: Kural 1294
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: You won’t sulk first and enjoy him after. So who will plan such things with you from now on, heart?

nodes.label: Kural 1295
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: My heart fears not having him, and when it has him it fears parting. Its suffering never ends.

nodes.label: Kural 1296
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: When I sat alone and thought, my heart stayed with me only to eat me up.

nodes.label: Kural 1297
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Caught up with this worthless, foolish heart that can’t forget him, I have forgotten even my modesty.

nodes.label: Kural 1298
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: My heart, in love with life, thinks it would be shameful to scorn him, and so it keeps thinking of his ways.

nodes.label: Kural 1299
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: In trouble, who will stand by you if your own heart won’t?

nodes.label: Kural 1300
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: If your own heart isn’t on your side, it is a small thing that strangers aren’t.

nodes.label: Kural 1301
nodes.speaker: friend
nodes.snippet: Don’t embrace him. Sulk, and let us see a little of the pain and sickness he goes through.

nodes.label: Kural 1302
nodes.speaker: friend
nodes.snippet: A sulk is like the right amount of salt. Drawing it out is like a little too much.

nodes.label: Kural 1303
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Not to embrace those who sulk with you is like bringing fresh pain to people already in distress.

nodes.label: Kural 1304
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Not to soothe those who sulk is like cutting a withered creeper at the root.

nodes.label: Kural 1305
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: What graces those of fine character is the sulking in the hearts of women with eyes like flowers.

nodes.label: Kural 1306
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Without the deep sulk and the light one, desire is like a fruit too ripe and a fruit too green.

nodes.label: Kural 1307
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: There is a pain even in sulking: the worry over whether union will be delayed.

nodes.label: Kural 1308
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: What is the use of suffering, when there is no lover to know you are suffering?

nodes.label: Kural 1309
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Water is sweet in the shade, and sulking is sweet with those who love you.

nodes.label: Kural 1310
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: My heart says we will join with the one who leaves a sulk to wither. That is only craving.

nodes.label: Kural 1311
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: All those who are women eat you up with their eyes, as common property. I won’t go near your chest, you philanderer.

nodes.label: Kural 1312
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: I was sulking when he sneezed. He knew I would say, “Live long.”

nodes.label: Kural 1313
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Even if I wear a flower from the branch she is angry. “You wear it to show some woman,” she says.

nodes.label: Kural 1314
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: “We love more than anyone,” I said, and she sulked: “Than who? Than who?”

nodes.label: Kural 1315
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: “We will not part in this life,” I said, and her eyes filled with tears.

nodes.label: Kural 1316
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: “I thought of you,” I said. “So why did you forget me?” she said, and she didn’t embrace me but got ready to sulk.

nodes.label: Kural 1317
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: I sneezed and she blessed me. Then she took it back and wept: “Who was thinking of you, that you sneezed?”

nodes.label: Kural 1318
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: I held back a sneeze and she wept: “Are you hiding from me that your own people are thinking of you?”

nodes.label: Kural 1319
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Even when I soothe her sulk she flares up: “So this is how you are with others too.”

nodes.label: Kural 1320
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Even if I just sit thinking and gazing at her, she flares up: “Who are you thinking of, looking at all of me like that?”

nodes.label: Kural 1321
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: He has done nothing wrong, yet sulking is what draws out his tenderness.

nodes.label: Kural 1322
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: The small hurt of sulking may dim his tenderness for a moment, but it comes back greater.

nodes.label: Kural 1323
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: Is there any heaven better than a lovers’ quarrel, between two people as blended as earth and water?

nodes.label: Kural 1324
nodes.speaker: she
nodes.snippet: In the very quarrel that keeps me clinging to him is the weapon that breaks my resolve.

nodes.label: Kural 1325
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Even when you have done nothing wrong, being kept from the soft shoulders of the one you love has a pleasure of its own.

nodes.label: Kural 1326
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Digesting a meal is sweeter than eating more. In desire, a quarrel is sweeter than making love.

nodes.label: Kural 1327
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: In a lovers’ quarrel, the one who loses has won. You see it when you come back together.

nodes.label: Kural 1328
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Will a quarrel bring back the sweetness of our lovemaking, the kind that left her forehead damp with sweat?

nodes.label: Kural 1329
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Let her go on sulking, this woman in bright jewels, and let the night run on while I plead.

nodes.label: Kural 1330
nodes.speaker: he
nodes.snippet: Sulking is the joy of desire, and the joy of sulking is the embrace that ends it, if you get that far.

nodes.label: Tiruvalluvar
nodes.desc: The poet of the Kural, who speaks in Parts 1 and 2.

nodes.label: He
nodes.desc: The man of Part 3, who speaks in the couplets on his love.

nodes.label: She
nodes.desc: The woman of Part 3, who speaks in most of its couplets.

nodes.label: The Friend
nodes.desc: Her friend in Part 3, who speaks to them both.

nodes.label: Righteousness
nodes.desc: The moral good as a whole, first of the three aims of life, which the Kural calls the surest profit and the only source of real delight.

nodes.label: Purity of Heart
nodes.desc: A mind without stain, which Kural 34 calls the whole of righteousness, all else being empty sound, and which one's company can keep or spoil.

nodes.label: Devotion
nodes.desc: Taking refuge at the feet of the Lord and praising him, which the opening chapter makes the only way across the sea of births and the only real use of learning.

nodes.label: Loving-kindness
nodes.desc: The warm goodwill of the heart towards others, the mēttā of Buddhism, which gives even one's bones for them, grows into friendship, and which the Kural calls the seat of life.

nodes.label: Compassion
nodes.desc: Care for every living thing, stranger and creature alike, which the Kural calls the wealth of wealths and the one true help, born of loving-kindness and nursed by wealth.

nodes.label: Cruelty
nodes.desc: Hardness of heart that feels nothing for other lives, so that a man oppresses the weak and forgets how he would tremble in their place.

nodes.label: Fear of Evil Deeds
nodes.desc: Dread of doing evil, to be feared more than fire, because ill deeds follow their author like his shadow and destroy him.

nodes.label: Self-Control
nodes.desc: Mastery of one's passions, temper and whole bearing, to be guarded as a treasure, which leads to heaven as its lack leads to endless darkness.

nodes.label: Control of the Five Senses
nodes.desc: Holding in the five senses as the goad holds the elephant or the tortoise draws in its limbs, the mark of the ascetic's might.

nodes.label: Humility
nodes.desc: Bending before others, which suits everyone, shines brightest in the rich, and is called the strength of the strong.

nodes.label: Good Conduct
nodes.desc: The steady behaviour proper to one's place, to be guarded above life itself, by which a man's family and standing are known.

nodes.label: Forgiveness
nodes.desc: Bearing injury and insult as the earth bears those who dig it, and better still forgetting them, which the Kural sets above fasting and above renunciation.

nodes.label: Revenge
nodes.desc: Paying back an injury, whose joy lasts only a day and which brings further evils down on the one who takes it.

nodes.label: Anger
nodes.desc: Hot displeasure that seeks to hurt, and that the Kural treats as the enemy of the one who feels it.

nodes.label: Enmity
nodes.desc: Settled hatred between persons or powers, not to be invited even in jest, which no study can remove from an enemy's heart.

nodes.label: Strife
nodes.desc: A quarrelsome spirit that delights in opposing others, the disease from which hate grows and from which all that is bitter springs.

nodes.label: Non-Injury
nodes.desc: Causing no pain to anyone, even for great gain or in return for malice, because one's own pain shows what it is to inflict it.
lexicon: treating others as you would like to be treated

nodes.label: Non-Killing
nodes.desc: Never taking life, ranked as the first of all righteous acts, above truthfulness, and binding even to save one’s own life.

nodes.label: Abstaining from Meat
nodes.desc: Refusing to eat flesh, because no one who fattens himself on another body can feel pity, and because the eater's demand is what keeps the killing going.

nodes.label: Austerity
nodes.desc: Bearing suffering patiently and hurting no life, which Kural 261 calls the whole of austerity, and by which, like gold in the fire, the austere shine the brighter.

nodes.label: Renunciation
nodes.desc: Giving up possessions and ties, since each thing let go is a grief escaped, and owning nothing is the law of those under vows.

nodes.label: Attachment
nodes.desc: Clinging to things and bonds, which grief in turn clings to, and which keeps the round of births turning until it is broken.

nodes.label: Craving
nodes.desc: Wanting itself, the seed of every birth, never filled, a trap that cheats a person, called here the greatest misery of all.

nodes.label: Desirelessness
nodes.desc: Wanting nothing, called the greatest wealth and a greatness that triumphs over all, which is freedom here and now.

nodes.label: Realisation of the Truth
nodes.desc: Seeing through appearances to the real, the liberating insight of chapter 36 that ends delusion and the need to be born again.

nodes.label: Delusion
nodes.desc: Taking the unreal for the real and the passing for the lasting, named with desire and anger as the root of all ills.

nodes.label: Grief
nodes.desc: Sorrow as the common lot of those who hold on to the world, which the Kural traces to attachment and desire.

nodes.label: Hospitality
nodes.desc: Receiving and feeding the guest before oneself, with a glad face, which the Kural makes the very purpose of setting up a home.

nodes.label: Charity
nodes.desc: Giving to those who have nothing and sharing one's food with them, with no hope of return, all other giving being only a kind of loan.

nodes.label: Generosity
nodes.desc: An open hand as a standing trait of a ruler or a man of good family, which draws kin and followers to him and which survives even shrinking means.

nodes.label: Helpfulness
nodes.desc: Keeping one’s means open to the whole community as a village tank or a fruit tree serves all, expecting no return, even at the cost of ruin.

nodes.label: Gratitude
nodes.desc: Holding a kindness far larger than it looks, weighing it by the need it met, and remembering the helper for life and in every birth.

nodes.label: Ingratitude
nodes.desc: Forgetting or destroying a kindness received, the one crime for which the Kural allows no redemption.
lexicon: biting the hand that feeds you

nodes.label: Miserliness
nodes.desc: Hoarding wealth without spending, giving or even enjoying it, which the Kural sets apart as a class of vice by itself.

nodes.label: Moderation
nodes.desc: Knowing the measure of things, so that giving and spending stay within one's wealth and eating stays within one's appetite.

nodes.label: Envy
nodes.desc: Pain at another’s good fortune, which needs no enemy to ruin the envious man and which drives the goddess of fortune from him.

nodes.label: Covetousness
nodes.desc: Reaching for wealth that belongs to another, which ruins the family, undoes a subtle mind and turns bitter in the enjoyment.

nodes.label: Fraud
nodes.desc: Scheming to cheat others of their property, a sin even as a thought, whose gains perish however fast they seem to grow.

nodes.label: Hypocrisy
nodes.desc: Wearing the look of holiness over an unrenounced heart, like a cow in a tiger's skin, a pretence at which the hypocrite's own body laughs.

nodes.label: Kind Speech
nodes.desc: Pleasant words from a sincere heart with a gracious look, rated above a generous gift and set beside harsh words as ripe fruit beside unripe.

nodes.label: Harsh Speech
nodes.desc: Hard and wounding words said to a person’s face, which is choosing the unripe fruit, and which bring even a ruler’s prosperity to an end.

nodes.label: Restraint of Speech
nodes.desc: Guarding the tongue above all else, since a single wounding word cancels a person's virtue and the burn of the tongue never heals.

nodes.label: Useless Words
nodes.desc: Words that bring no profit to anyone, which reveal a man's own emptiness and make him chaff among men.

nodes.label: Slander
nodes.desc: Speaking ill of someone behind his back, worse than open wrongdoing because it smiles in front and vilifies behind.

nodes.label: Truthfulness
nodes.desc: Speech free of any taint of harm, so that even an untruth bringing pure good counts as truth, and the highest thing the poet has seen in this world.

nodes.label: Falsehood
nodes.desc: Telling lies, which burns one's own conscience, is worse than dying, and adds one more wrong to any other.

nodes.label: Eloquence
nodes.desc: Power in speech that binds friends, charms enemies and cannot be answered, used in few and well chosen words.

nodes.label: Tact
nodes.desc: Weighing the hearers and the occasion before speaking, so that wisdom goes to the wise and fools are answered at their own level.

nodes.label: Courage Before an Audience
nodes.desc: Facing a learned assembly without trembling, a rarer thing than courage in battle, without which learning is a sword in a eunuch's hand.

nodes.label: Discretion
nodes.desc: Keeping one's plans and pleasures and other people's secrets to oneself until the work is done, a failure of which ruins the shallow and marks the base.

nodes.label: Frank Counsel
nodes.desc: Telling those in one’s care what is right though they resist, the minister’s duty to a foolish ruler and the true friend’s purpose.

nodes.label: Openness to Rebuke
nodes.desc: Keeping close those who can reprove one and bearing words bitter to the ear, without which a ruler falls even with no enemy at all.

nodes.label: Understanding
nodes.desc: Clear practical intelligence that curbs the senses, sifts the true from the false in every saying, and guards a man like a fortress.

nodes.label: Foresight
nodes.desc: Knowing what is coming and being armed for it beforehand, set against the fool's rush into what ought to be feared.

nodes.label: Worldly Wisdom
nodes.desc: Moving in step with the ways of the world, a part of wisdom without which book learning still leaves a man a fool.

nodes.label: Self-Examination
nodes.desc: Looking at one's own faults as one looks at others', treating a small failing as huge, and correcting oneself before judging anyone else.

nodes.label: Deliberation
nodes.desc: Reckoning cost, gain and method with trusted men before undertaking anything, since a fool is one who acts first and thinks afterwards.

nodes.label: Knowing One's Strength
nodes.desc: Weighing the task, one's own force and the force of enemy and allies before acting, and not overstepping that limit.
lexicon: not biting off more than you can chew

nodes.label: Vigilance
nodes.desc: Never relaxing one's guard or forgetting one's purpose, the one thing that puts everything else within reach.

nodes.label: Complacency
nodes.desc: Forgetful unguardedness born of elation at success, worse than rage, which kills glory as poverty kills the understanding.

nodes.label: Folly
nodes.desc: Throwing away what profits and holding to what harms, and inclining to what is unbecoming, a fault that can sit with great learning.

nodes.label: Conceited Folly
nodes.desc: The shallow man's belief that he is wise, which refuses advice, pretends to what it lacks and brings on troubles no enemy could devise.

nodes.label: Ignorance
nodes.desc: Never having studied, which leaves a man a wasteland, shamed before the wise, and no better than beasts beside the learned.

nodes.label: Reading Intentions
nodes.desc: Divining from face and eye what is in another's heart before it is spoken, a gift rated as godlike in a man at one's side.

nodes.label: Arrogance
nodes.desc: Haughty self-regard and the pride of I and mine, the admiring of oneself that the wise cut away.
lexicon: thinking you are better than others

nodes.label: Energy
nodes.desc: Inward spirit and drive, the one real possession, which measures a man's fortunes as the water measures the flower.

nodes.label: Sloth
nodes.desc: Laziness with its companions, procrastination, forgetfulness and sleep, which puts out the light of a family and brings it under its foes.

nodes.label: Exertion
nodes.desc: Sustained personal labour that finishes what it starts, the mother of prosperity, which pays its wages even when god and fate stand against it.

nodes.label: Resolve
nodes.desc: Firmness of will in carrying a decision through, the only real measure of achievement, which does not waver once the matter is settled.

nodes.label: Fortitude
nodes.desc: Keeping heart when trouble comes, meeting it with a smile and taking it as part of the law of things, so that the troubles themselves give way.

nodes.label: Equanimity
nodes.desc: An even temper that neither swells at good fortune nor sinks at bad, because the wise take both as they come.

nodes.label: Aspiration
nodes.desc: Setting one's aims high, so that even failure keeps its glory, which the Kural makes a test of greatness.

nodes.label: Courage
nodes.desc: Fearlessness as one of a ruler's four essentials, which does not extend to failing to fear what should be feared (Kural 428).

nodes.label: Valour
nodes.desc: The warrior's fierce courage that delights in wounds and gives life for fame, and that is sharpened, says Kural 773, by generosity to the fallen.

nodes.label: Cowardice
nodes.desc: Fear that fails a person at the moment of need, which makes fortresses useless and is a joy to his enemies.

nodes.label: Impartiality
nodes.desc: Giving each his due, friend or foe, and inclining to neither side in one's own mind, like the straight beam of a balance.

nodes.label: Just Rule
nodes.desc: A sceptre that leans to neither side, protecting the people and punishing wrong after careful inquiry, on which rains and all learning depend.

nodes.label: Tyranny
nodes.desc: A ruler's oppression of his people and abuse of office, called worse than murder and like highway robbery, which the tears of the oppressed wear away.

nodes.label: Severity
nodes.desc: Ruling by fear with excessive punishment and harsh words, which files away the iron of power; the rod should be raised sharply but brought down gently (Kural 562).

nodes.label: Accessibility
nodes.desc: A ruler’s being easy to approach and see, the mark of a good one, whose lack ruins him even with no enemy.
lexicon: a boss you can talk to

nodes.label: Loyalty
nodes.desc: Standing by one's master at any cost, as the envoy who does his duty under threat of death or the soldier who would die to bring tears to his chief's eyes.

nodes.label: Purity of Action
nodes.desc: Using only clean means in any undertaking, refusing what good men condemn even to save one's mother from starving, since gain by guile is water in an unbaked pot.

nodes.label: Reverence for the Great
nodes.desc: Taking care never to slight men of power or holy strength, whose displeasure destroys even rulers and gods.

nodes.label: Cherishing Kin
nodes.desc: Keeping one's relations close by shared wealth, sweet words and freedom from anger, which the Kural calls the very use of prosperity.

nodes.label: Intimacy
nodes.desc: The ease of long friendship, taking a friend’s liberties and even real damage in good part, out of loving-kindness that does not change.

nodes.label: Fair-Weather Friendship
nodes.desc: Friendship kept only for what it yields, fawning when useful and leaving when not, compared with prostitutes and thieves and a horse that throws its rider in battle.
lexicon: friends who only call when they need something

nodes.label: False Friendship
nodes.desc: An enemy's show of friendship, smiling, bending and weeping while hate waits in the heart, a weapon hidden in joined hands.

nodes.label: Treachery
nodes.desc: Enmity inside one’s own house or circle, which splits what looks whole and strikes at the moment of weakness.

nodes.label: Greatness
nodes.desc: Doing what others cannot, joined with modesty, humility towards all and the screening of others' failings.

nodes.label: Littleness
nodes.desc: A small nature that cannot honour the great, turns insolent in good fortune, boasts of its merits and talks scandal.

nodes.label: Baseness
nodes.desc: The degraded state of those who look human but have no conscience, moved only by fear and appetite, who give only under blows.

nodes.label: Worth
nodes.desc: Complete moral character, resting on five pillars of loving-kindness, shame, helpfulness, considerateness and truthfulness, whose loss the earth itself could not bear.

nodes.label: Courtesy
nodes.desc: Good manners shown to everyone, friend or foe, never discourteous even in jest, by which the world goes smoothly.

nodes.label: Considerateness
nodes.desc: The kindly eye that indulges those before it and puts up with their faults, without which eyes are mere sores, and which must not override duty.

nodes.label: Nobility of Birth
nodes.desc: The good conduct, truthfulness, sense of shame and open hand expected of those born in a good family, whose smallest fault shows like the spot on the moon.

nodes.label: Honour
nodes.desc: Refusal to sink below oneself, even to preserve one's life, so that those who lose it are like hair shaven from the head.

nodes.label: Sense of Shame
nodes.desc: Shrinking from what is unworthy, the mark that sets one person above another and is held dearer than life, quite apart from the shyness of good women (Kural 1011).

nodes.label: Servility
nodes.desc: Fawning on those who despise one for the sake of a living, counted worse than death, which poverty can force even on the well born.

nodes.label: Refusal to Beg
nodes.desc: Dread of asking for anything, preferring thin gruel earned by one's own hands, a dignity the whole universe is too small to hold.

nodes.label: Chastity
nodes.desc: A woman's firmness of fidelity, guarded from within rather than by confinement, which the Kural calls her greatest strength.

nodes.label: Wifely Virtue
nodes.desc: The excellence of a good wife, spending within her husband's means and tending him and their name, without which all other blessings come to nothing.

nodes.label: Adultery
nodes.desc: Desiring or going to another man's wife, which the Kural calls the worst folly, bringing hatred, sin, fear and shame that never leave the adulterer.

nodes.label: Lust
nodes.desc: Bodily appetite as a vice of unguarded men, whether it makes a ruler its slave or drowns fools in the arms of prostitutes.

nodes.label: Submission to One's Wife
nodes.desc: A man's abject doting on or fear of his wife, which the Kural says costs him esteem, duty to friends and great deeds.

nodes.label: Drunkenness
nodes.desc: Addiction to toddy, which forfeits honour and even a mother's regard and makes the drinker as one asleep or dead.

nodes.label: Gambling
nodes.desc: The passion for dice, a baited hook that loses a hundred for each gained, consuming wealth, name and honesty, and growing with its losses.

nodes.label: Desire
nodes.desc: The consuming desire between man and woman, vast as the sea and tender as a flower, which Part 3 treats as the supreme joy and the deepest pain.

nodes.label: Being Smitten
nodes.desc: The first blow of a woman's beauty on the man who sees her, felt as a goddess, a war and death itself.

nodes.label: Dread of Parting
nodes.desc: The inability to bear the thought of parting, felt before he has gone, so that even his embrace saddens her.

nodes.label: Pining
nodes.desc: Wasting grief in the absence of the beloved, hidden at first and then beyond hiding, that wells up like a spring and keeps her awake all night.

nodes.label: Longing to Meet
nodes.desc: Eager impatience for the beloved's return and for reunion, counting the days and living on the hope of meeting.

nodes.label: One-Sided Love
nodes.desc: The anguish of loving one who does not love back, when desire is a load on one end of the carrying pole alone.
lexicon: loving someone who doesn't love you
they don't feel the same way

nodes.label: Loving Remembrance
nodes.desc: Keeping the beloved in mind, a memory that both sustains life and burns, and is sweeter than toddy.
lexicon: thinking about them all the time

nodes.label: Bashfulness
nodes.desc: A woman’s shrinking modesty in love, the ornament of her look, which desire strains to breaking point.

nodes.label: Reserve
nodes.desc: Composed self-possession in love, which keeps feeling hidden and refuses to run after a deserter, and which the axe of desire breaks down.

nodes.label: Sulking
nodes.desc: The sulk or quarrel between lovers (also ஊடல்), feigned or half meant, called the salt of love, whose sweetness lies in the embrace that ends it.

nodes.label: Jealous Sulking
nodes.desc: A lover's quick suspicion that the other's heart is shared, which finds a rival in a garland, a sneeze or an innocent compliment.

nodes.label: Worry
nodes.desc: A mind that runs ahead to what may come and won’t settle, which Kural 7 says is hard to remove and which Kural 1072 says only the base are free of.

nodes.label: Fear
nodes.desc: Being afraid, whether of people, of harm or of speaking up. The book sorts it rather than bans it. Fearing what should be feared is wisdom (Kural 428), yet there is no fort for those who are afraid (Kural 534).

nodes.label: Guilt
nodes.desc: Your own heart knowing what you did and burning you for it (Kural 293). No outward show helps when the heart sinks into a fault it knows (Kural 272).

nodes.label: Humiliation
nodes.desc: Being brought low in someone’s sight, by scorn, by having to ask or by having nothing. Scorn hurts even in fun (Kural 995), yet having nothing is no disgrace where worth holds (Kural 988).

nodes.label: Regret
nodes.desc: Looking back and crying “What have I done?”, the word Kural 655 uses and Kural 535 gives to one who failed to guard in advance, when the blow lands and it is too late.

nodes.label: Loneliness
nodes.desc: Having no one with you. Part 3 knows it at midnight when all else sleeps (Kural 1167, Kural 1168), and Kural 1158 calls a town without your own people painful. Yet Kural 814 says it is better than false company.

nodes.label: Hurt
nodes.desc: The wound left by what someone said or did, worst when they were close. A word’s scar never heals (Kural 129), and being deserted in your ruin burns the heart even at the hour of death (Kural 799).
lexicon: can't get over what they said

nodes.label: Distrust
nodes.desc: Not being able to believe in someone. The book counts it a suffering in itself. Doubting someone you have come to trust brings pain that doesn’t end (Kural 510), and suspicion once in place is hard to clear (Kural 693).

nodes.label: Losing Heart
nodes.desc: The sinking of spirit when trouble comes or a task looks too hard, which Kural 611 warns against by name and chapter 63 meets head on. It isn’t failing, since aiming high holds its worth even then (Kural 596).

nodes.label: Helplessness
nodes.desc: Seeing no way out, no shore and no raft. Those who suffer and can’t bear it have their tears (Kural 555), and fate gets there before your plan (Kural 380). The book’s reply is effort, without promising the result (Kural 619).

nodes.label: Restlessness
nodes.desc: A mind that won’t settle or sleep. Part 3 knows it through the night (Kural 1179, Kural 1252), and Kural 337 sees it in those who think ten million thoughts with no promise of the next moment.

nodes.label: Elation
nodes.desc: The high spirits of great delight, which feel like strength (Kural 539). The book fears them for what they stop you watching, and calls that carelessness worse than boundless rage (Kural 531).

nodes.label: The Lord
nodes.desc: The First Lord from whom the world begins, whose knowledge is pure, who wants nothing and rejects nothing, praised in the opening chapter without any sectarian name.

nodes.label: Rain
nodes.desc: Rain as the sustainer of the world, on which food, the sea, sacrifice, charity and right conduct itself all depend.

nodes.label: The Three Aims of Life
nodes.desc: The scheme of three ends of life, righteousness, wealth and desire, which the Kural's three Parts follow and which some couplets name together.

nodes.label: Family Life
nodes.desc: Life in the home as the ground of all other paths, with its five duties, held to be no lesser road than asceticism.

nodes.label: Offspring
nodes.desc: Children as the highest blessing, in the sweetness of their touch and speech and in the worth that parents and children owe one another.

nodes.label: Speech
nodes.desc: The word as a power in itself, in which rise and ruin lie, and by which a person's birth and nature are known.

nodes.label: Learning
nodes.desc: Study as the eyes of the mind, an imperishable treasure that travels with one through every land and birth, and that must be lived by.

nodes.label: Listening to the Wise
nodes.desc: Learning by ear from the wise, the first of all riches, a staff to the unschooled and a support in trouble.

nodes.label: Wealth
nodes.desc: Money and property, the second aim of life, which lights every dark place and cuts down pride, provided it is gained without evil.

nodes.label: Poverty
nodes.desc: Having nothing, a curse that kills dignity, silences wisdom and robs sleep, so that the poor man’s truest words carry no weight.

nodes.label: Begging
nodes.desc: Asking help of others, which chapter 106 allows of those who give without humbling, and without which the glory of the generous would not exist.

nodes.label: Glory
nodes.desc: Lasting renown earned chiefly by giving, the one thing that does not die, without which it would be better not to have been born.

nodes.label: Impermanence
nodes.desc: The passing of wealth, body and life, which should be seen early so that good is done before the tongue fails.

nodes.label: Rebirth
nodes.desc: The round of births and the next world that await the soul, in which merit, learning and guilt are carried forward and of which desire is the seed.

nodes.label: Liberation
nodes.desc: Freedom from birth, the end of the ascetic path, reached by breaking all attachment and realising the truth.

nodes.label: Fate
nodes.desc: The mighty power that allots and withholds, gets ahead of every plan, and makes even resolve and intelligence rise and fall with it.

nodes.label: The Fruits of Action
nodes.desc: The return of good and evil deeds upon their doer, the shadow that follows him through this life and others.

nodes.label: Rulership
nodes.desc: The office of the ruler and its marks, the six possessions and the qualities that make a ruler a lion among rulers.

nodes.label: The Country
nodes.desc: What makes a land great, abundant harvests, freedom from plague and invasion, unity within and a worthy ruler.

nodes.label: Fortresses
nodes.desc: Defensive works and strong places, natural and built, with their needs of height, stores and brave defenders.

nodes.label: The Army
nodes.desc: The fighting force as a possession of the ruler, with its tradition, discipline, pay and leaders.

nodes.label: War and Enemies
nodes.desc: The handling of enemies and the making of war, when to fight, whom to avoid, how to divide foes and how to subdue them in time.

nodes.label: Using Spies
nodes.desc: The ruler’s use of spies, one of his two eyes, with its checking of one report against another.

nodes.label: Enterprise
nodes.desc: Carrying a chosen undertaking through, what to weigh, whom to learn from, how to use one task for another, and when to hurry.

nodes.label: Time
nodes.desc: The right moment as a strategic force, by which the weak can conquer, and for which the wise wait without hurry before they strike.

nodes.label: Place
nodes.desc: The choice of ground, on which the weak may beat the strong, as the crocodile rules in deep water and nowhere else.

nodes.label: Testing People
nodes.desc: Proving a person's character before giving trust, office or friendship, by acts rather than appearances, and then not doubting the one who has passed.

nodes.label: Friendship
nodes.desc: The bond between friends as the rarest protection, waxing like the moon, built on the union of hearts and existing to restrain and uplift.
lexicon: having people you can rely on

nodes.label: Company
nodes.desc: The people one moves among, who colour the mind as soil colours water, so that the worthy are to be sought and the petty avoided.

nodes.label: The Family Line
nodes.desc: The family as a line to be kept up and raised by a man's labour, which falls through sloth and whose burden falls on those who can bear it.

nodes.label: Agriculture
nodes.desc: Farming as the chief of all work, the linchpin of society, which alone is free of dependence and feeds even those who have renounced.

nodes.label: Health
nodes.desc: The care of the body by eating only after digestion and in measure, and the physician's measured cure of disease.

nodes.label: The Joy of Love
nodes.desc: The happiness of lovers together, the third aim of life, in which all five senses are filled and which outdoes even the world of the lotus-eyed one.

nodes.label: Separation of Lovers
nodes.desc: The parting of lovers, usually his going away for conquest or wealth, which is the setting of most of the later chapters of Part 3.

nodes.label: Gossip About Lovers
nodes.desc: The village’s talk about two lovers, which feeds the desire it would shame, as manure and water feed a plant.

nodes.label: The Beloved's Beauty
nodes.desc: The lover’s praise of the woman’s charms, beyond flowers and moon, and tender past the aṉiccam and the swan’s down.

nodes.label: The Signs of Love
nodes.desc: The silent language of lovers, the stolen glance, the look at the ground and the half-smile, by which they say what the mouth need not.

nodes.label: Householder
nodes.desc: The married head of a home, who supports those on the other paths of life and is held to be the equal of any ascetic.

nodes.label: Ascetic
nodes.desc: One who has left home and the senses behind for a life of vows, whose greatness cannot be measured and whose wrath cannot be borne.

nodes.label: Sage
nodes.desc: The keeper of scripture, whom Kural 30 defines by tenderness towards all life, and whose place rests on his conduct and on the ruler’s protection. The Brahmin (பார்ப்பான்) of Kural 134 comes under this entry.

nodes.label: The Ruler
nodes.desc: The one who rules a realm, to whom the greater part of Part 2 is addressed.

nodes.label: Minister
nodes.desc: The ruler’s adviser, skilled in planning, in dividing allies and reuniting enemies, and bound to tell him what is right.

nodes.label: Envoy
nodes.desc: The ambassador who carries a ruler’s message abroad, and who must have loving-kindness, learning and few words, and stay true to his master even under threat of death.

nodes.label: Spy
nodes.desc: The ruler’s secret agent, disguised and unsuspected, who keeps his secret whatever is done to him.

nodes.label: Commander
nodes.desc: The chief who leads soldiers, without whom there is no army, and whose tears are what the soldier would die for.

nodes.label: Soldier
nodes.desc: The fighting man, veteran or hero, who counts a day without wounds as wasted.

nodes.label: Courtier
nodes.desc: One who lives close to a ruler and depends on his favour, and who must stand neither too near nor too far, as at a fire.
lexicon: someone working for a powerful boss

nodes.label: Officer of State
nodes.desc: The servant of the state entrusted with a task, chosen by testing and overseen daily by the ruler.

nodes.label: Subject
nodes.desc: The people under a ruler, who look to his sceptre, pay his taxes and whose tears wear away his wealth.

nodes.label: Friend
nodes.desc: One bound to another by friendship, who turns him from wrong and stands by him in misfortune.

nodes.label: Enemy
nodes.desc: The foe, in war or at heart, to be weighed, avoided, divided or overcome in due time.

nodes.label: Kinsman
nodes.desc: A relation, whose constancy in adversity is the mark of kin and whose quarrels can be healed.

nodes.label: The Great Ones
nodes.desc: Persons of spiritual or worldly might set above others, whose friendship is a strength and whose offence is a death warrant.

nodes.label: Scholar
nodes.desc: The learned man, whose coming brings joy, for whom every land is home, and who is rated above the unlearned of any birth.

nodes.label: Orator
nodes.desc: One who addresses an assembly, whom chapters 72 and 73 instruct to weigh his words and to hold his nerve.

nodes.label: Physician
nodes.desc: The healer who measures patient, disease and season before he treats, one of the four on whom all cure depends.

nodes.label: Farmer
nodes.desc: The ploughman, the linchpin of society, who alone lives by his own bread and gives to others without refusing.

nodes.label: Beggar
nodes.desc: One who lives by asking, whose lot the Kural pities and whose scowl at a refusal it forbids.

nodes.label: Guest
nodes.desc: The visitor who comes to the home, whose honour is the householder’s duty and whose heart a cold look can break.

nodes.label: Husband
nodes.desc: A man in relation to his wife, tended by the good wife, and warned in chapter 91 against submission to her.

nodes.label: Wife
nodes.desc: The woman of the house, the life partner of chapter 6, on whose virtue the home’s worth rests.

nodes.label: Parent
nodes.desc: Father or mother in what they owe a child and gain from one, to fit him for the front rank and to hear him called worthy.

nodes.label: Child
nodes.desc: A son or child, whose worth is the joy of parents, and who repays a father by making the world ask what he did to deserve him.

nodes.label: Prostitute
nodes.desc: The woman who sells her embrace for gold, shown in chapter 92 only as a danger to the man who seeks her.

nodes.label: Lover
nodes.desc: Man or woman in love, before or after marriage, who speaks through all of Part 3 or is spoken of there.

nodes.label: Confidante
nodes.desc: The woman's maid and intimate friend in Part 3, to whom she speaks and who sometimes speaks for her or gives counsel.

nodes.label: Village Folk
nodes.desc: The neighbours of Part 3 whose talk, blame and pity surround the lovers, and who are always a little wrong about them.

nodes.label: A friend has let you down
nodes.desc: A friend of long standing has hurt or damaged you, and the Kural pulls two ways, between bearing with old friends and dropping false ones.
nodes.silent: The book pulls two ways. Chapter 81 says to bear the faults of old friends. Chapters 82 and 83 say some faults can’t be borne and the friendship must go. It doesn’t say which this is.

nodes.label: Your friends vanished when things got hard
nodes.desc: You have hit trouble and those you counted on have gone, which the Kural treats as a useful rod for measuring who your friends really were.
keywords: nobody called when i lost everything
everyone left me when i needed them
friends only around when things are good
finding out who my real friends are

nodes.label: Deciding whether to trust someone new
nodes.desc: Someone new wants your confidence, and the Kural says to weigh family, character and associates first, since trust without testing brings endless ills.
keywords: how to know if someone is trustworthy
new friend seems too good to be true
should i open up to them

nodes.label: The people around you are a bad influence
nodes.desc: Your circle is pulling you down, and the Kural says the mind takes the colour of its company as water takes the character of its soil.
keywords: my friends are a bad influence
hanging out with the wrong people

nodes.label: Someone is friendly to your face but working against you
nodes.desc: Someone smiles at you and means you harm, whether a rival or one of your own, and the Kural fears this more than an open enemy, like a cobra in the hut.
keywords: talks about me behind my back

nodes.label: Someone close tells you a hard truth
nodes.desc: A friend or adviser has told you what you did not want to hear, and the Kural says such people are your protection and that without them you fall.
nodes.silent: These lines are about a friend who rebukes you when you go wrong, to turn you back. They aren’t about being belittled or worn down, and they don’t ask you to take that as the truth.

nodes.label: A friend is in trouble and needs you
nodes.desc: A friend has hit misfortune, and the Kural says true friendship moves as fast as a hand to a slipping garment.
keywords: my friend is going through a hard time
should i drop everything for a friend

nodes.label: You need someone wiser to guide you
nodes.desc: You want an older or wiser person beside you, and the Kural calls finding one the rarest good fortune and a strength above all others.
keywords: who should i go to for advice

nodes.label: Someone hurt or insulted you and you want to hit back
nodes.desc: You have been wronged or run down and want payback, and the Kural says the joy of it lasts a day.
keywords: people saying bad things about me
nodes.silent: It offers no way to heal what was done to you, and it doesn’t say the wrong was small. What it says is that revenge turns back on the one who takes it.

nodes.label: You are furious with someone
nodes.desc: Anger has you in its grip, and the Kural says that whoever the offender is, the anger will burn you and your own first.
nodes.silent: It speaks of what anger does to the one who holds it. It doesn’t ask what caused your anger, and it doesn’t say the cause was small.

nodes.label: Someone keeps picking a fight with you
nodes.desc: A neighbour or colleague keeps provoking you, and the Kural says not to return it, and that a talent for avoiding strife leaves no one wishing your fall.
keywords: a colleague looking for a fight
nodes.silent: These lines say to turn aside from strife and stop there. They give no remedy for someone who keeps provoking you, and turning aside isn’t the same as putting up with harm.

nodes.label: Someone else's success is eating at you
nodes.desc: Another's good fortune pains you, and the Kural says that pain needs no enemy's help to ruin you.
keywords: everyone is doing better than me
colleague got promoted instead of me

nodes.label: You said something hurtful and can't take it back
nodes.desc: Your words have wounded someone, and the Kural says that a burn heals in time but the wound from the tongue stays raw.
nodes.silent: It offers no way to take words back. It says the scar from the tongue never heals, and it doesn’t say the other person will forgive you.

nodes.label: You are tempted to cut a corner for money
nodes.desc: There is easy money in bending the rules, and the Kural says not to touch it, since such gain perishes and honest poverty is better.

nodes.label: Wondering whether a lie would do less harm
nodes.desc: You are weighing a lie against the truth, and the Kural's test is harm, truth being speech free of evil, and only a falsehood bringing pure good passing as truth.

nodes.label: You are drawn to someone who is married
nodes.desc: You are tempted by another's spouse, and the Kural names four things that will never leave you if you yield, hatred, sin, fear and shame.
keywords: in love with my friend's wife

nodes.label: Getting ahead means losing your self-respect
nodes.desc: Keeping your place means bowing to those who scorn you, and the Kural asks what anyone gains by following those who scorn them.
keywords: sucking up to keep my job
being treated like dirt at work
do i quit or swallow my pride
nodes.silent: It doesn’t say how to keep your job and your self-respect when you can’t have both. It asks what following those who scorn you wins, and it sets honour above gain. It doesn’t weigh what leaving would cost you.

nodes.label: You did something you are ashamed of
nodes.desc: You have done what you now regret, and the Kural's counsel is plain, avoid what makes you cry out what have I done, and if you did it, do not do it again.
keywords: how to live with what i did
nodes.silent: It offers no pardon and no way to undo what was done. Its counsel is short: the words say don’t do the like again, and Parimelazhagar reads them as don’t go on grieving.

nodes.label: Your work goes unrecognised
nodes.desc: You are overlooked for your looks or your standing, or your diligence is resented, and the Kural says the one who slights such a worker is the one who loses.

nodes.label: Something you want to do feels impossible
nodes.desc: A task looks beyond you and you are tempted to drop it, and the Kural says labour gives the strength and that unfinished work is what the world does not forgive.

nodes.label: You tried hard and failed
nodes.desc: Your effort did not pay off, and the Kural says the lack of a favouring fate is no shame, and that high aims keep their glory even when they fail.

nodes.label: You keep putting things off
nodes.desc: You are leaving for tomorrow what matters, and the Kural counts delay among the pleasure boats of those bound to perish and urges good works before the tongue fails.
keywords: leaving things to the last minute

nodes.label: Everything is going wrong at once
nodes.desc: Trouble has come from every side, and the Kural speaks of holding steady through what work and want bring.
keywords: lost my job and everything fell apart
nodes.silent: It doesn’t promise things will ease, and it says little to someone with no strength left. Parimelazhagar gives this answer for trouble met at your work, from god, want or bodily strain. It isn’t about harm someone is doing to you.

nodes.label: Deciding whether to start a business or big project
nodes.desc: You are thinking of taking on a venture, and the Kural says to reckon cost, loss and profit first, and to avoid what risks the capital itself.
keywords: quit my job to start a company

nodes.label: You have taken on more than you can handle
nodes.desc: You have overreached, and the Kural warns that even peacock feathers will break the axle if the load is great, and that the one at the treetop must not climb on.
keywords: burnt out from taking on too much

nodes.label: You are not sure whether now is the right time
nodes.desc: You are choosing between acting and waiting, and the Kural says to hold still like the stork and then strike without hesitating when the moment comes.
keywords: when should i make my move
should i wait or act now

nodes.label: Choosing the right person for a job
nodes.desc: You must pick someone for a task, and the Kural says to choose for knowledge and staying power rather than fondness, and then to leave them in charge.
keywords: giving a job to a relative

nodes.label: You have power over other people
nodes.desc: You manage, judge or discipline others, and the Kural says to make any penalty fit, to stay approachable, and to imagine yourself trembling before someone stronger.

nodes.label: You depend on a powerful boss
nodes.desc: Your living hangs on someone above you, and the Kural says to stay near but not too near, as with a fire, and to speak to their mood without presuming on favour.
keywords: keeping on the right side of my boss
nodes.silent: Chapter 70 is a minister’s guide to staying safe near a quarrelsome ruler. That chapter doesn’t ask you to bear cruelty, and it doesn’t say how to answer it. Elsewhere the book condemns rulers who torment people.

nodes.label: You are up against someone stronger
nodes.desc: A stronger rival stands against you, and the Kural says not to strive with the powerful, and to fight only on ground that favours you.
nodes.silent: This is advice for a contest between rivals. If someone stronger is hurting you, it doesn’t say what to do.

nodes.label: You have to speak in front of people
nodes.desc: You must address a room and you are afraid, and the Kural says to study the audience, master the matter and not let your learning die of fear.
keywords: scared to speak up at work

nodes.label: You are arguing with someone who will not listen
nodes.desc: You are trying to reason with a person sure he is right, and the Kural says the one who tries to open a fool's eyes is a fool himself.

nodes.label: Success is going to your head
nodes.desc: Things are going well and you feel above it all, and the Kural says to stay modest in prosperity and to remember those who fell through carelessness.
keywords: letting success go to my head

nodes.label: You are spending more than you earn
nodes.desc: Money is going out faster than it comes in, and the Kural says a narrow inflow does no harm so long as the outflow is not wider.
nodes.silent: It speaks of keeping what goes out within what comes in. It has nothing on debt you already owe, or on how to get clear of it.

nodes.label: You are struggling to make ends meet
nodes.desc: Poverty is wearing you down, and the Kural does not soften it, saying it kills dignity, robs sleep and brings many other miseries.
nodes.silent: It offers no practical way out. It says only poverty hurts like poverty, that there is no sleep in it, and that many miseries settle there. Some lines on the poor are harsh. Parimelazhagar says a body should be kept, even by begging.

nodes.label: You have to ask someone for money
nodes.desc: Need has driven you to ask, and the Kural says to ask only of those who give gladly, never of those who dodge.
keywords: too proud to ask for help
nodes.silent: This is never made easy. Chapter 106 says you may ask those who give gladly. Chapter 107 dreads the asking itself, even from them. Parimelazhagar says a body should be kept, even this way. It offers little for a refusal.

nodes.label: Someone in need asks you for help
nodes.desc: Someone in need is at your door, and the Kural says the noble never say “I have nothing”, and that a giver’s heart is not glad until the asker smiles.
keywords: a friend asked me for money

nodes.label: You have money and it brings you nothing
nodes.desc: You have saved plenty but neither enjoy nor share it, and the Kural says wealth kept this way is of use to no one.
keywords: what's the point of all this money
nodes.silent: It judges a life like this only from outside, and harshly. It doesn’t describe how it feels from within, or say the feeling will lift. What it does offer is giving and sharing, which it calls a joy.

nodes.label: Your drinking is getting out of hand
nodes.desc: Drink is taking over, and the Kural says you are spending your money to lose your senses and that you cannot hide it from those around you.
nodes.silent: It offers no cure and no way of stopping. It condemns: liquor costs you your wealth, your glory and your senses, and those around you see through it. It doesn’t say what to do when you can’t stop.

nodes.label: You cannot stop gambling
nodes.desc: You keep going back to the table, and the Kural says the win itself is the baited hook and that the passion grows with the losses.
nodes.silent: It offers no cure. It says the win is a hook, that the love of gambling grows with each loss, and that it takes your wealth, your good name and your compassion. It doesn’t say how to stop.

nodes.label: Your eating is harming your health
nodes.desc: Your eating habits are making you unwell, and the Kural says to eat moderately and only after the last meal is digested, for disease seeks the glutton.
nodes.silent: It speaks of measure, and mostly of eating too much. It says too little also brings disease, but it has nothing for someone who can’t control their eating.

nodes.label: However much you have, you want more
nodes.desc: Each thing gained leaves you wanting the next, and the Kural says desire is never filled and that only giving it up brings peace.

nodes.label: Wondering whether to stop eating meat
nodes.desc: You are uneasy about eating animals, and the Kural says that if no one bought flesh none would sell it, and that feeling the creature's pain ends the appetite.

nodes.label: Wanting to do right by your children
nodes.desc: You are trying to raise your children well, and the Kural says a father's debt is to fit his son for the front rank, and that to be outshone by him is a joy.
keywords: how to be a good parent
giving my kids a good education
what do i owe my kids
my child is smarter than me

nodes.label: You have fallen out with a relative
nodes.desc: Someone in your family has broken with you, and the Kural says to remove the cause and he will return, and to accept him back, but with caution.

nodes.label: You are carrying the whole family on your shoulders
nodes.desc: Everyone leans on you, and the Kural says the burden falls on those who can bear it, that they have no off season, and pities the body that takes the strain.
nodes.silent: It offers no rest, and it doesn’t say how to set the load down. It honours the one who carries and sees what the carrying costs, and it goes no further.

nodes.label: You have just fallen for someone
nodes.desc: Someone has caught your heart and you cannot read them yet, and the Kural's lovers live on glances and on eyes that agree before any word.
nodes.silent: It gives no advice here. Part 3 only sings what a lover feels, and the looks of two people who both want this. It isn’t a way of reading someone who hasn’t said so.

nodes.label: People are gossiping about your relationship
nodes.desc: Your love has become public talk, and Part 3 shows such talk only feeding desire, as manure and water feed a plant.
nodes.silent: It doesn’t say how to stop the talk, or what to do if it puts you at risk. Part 3 only shows such talk feeding desire and not ending it.

nodes.label: Your partner is away for a long time
nodes.desc: Your partner has gone for work or duty, and Part 3 knows the counted days, the evening that comes like an executioner, and the day that passes like seven.
nodes.silent: Its only comfort is memory, and it admits that can hurt too: “even remembering burns my heart.” It doesn’t shorten the wait.

nodes.label: You love someone who doesn't love you back
nodes.desc: You love and are not loved in return, and the Kural says desire is sweet only on both sides, like a load balanced on a pole.
keywords: in love with someone who doesn't care
they just see me as a friend
nodes.silent: Part 3 speaks in the lover’s own voice. It knows this pain, and that desire on one side only is like a load on one end of a pole. It offers no cure, and it doesn’t say how the pain ends.

nodes.label: You can't let go of someone who has left you
nodes.desc: Someone has gone and your heart will not accept it, and the woman of chapter 125 argues with her heart that keeping him there only wastes her further.
keywords: still in love with my ex
how to move on from a breakup
nodes.silent: It doesn’t say how to stop. She tells her heart it is foolish, and in the next chapter her reserve breaks down. This is a woman left by a living lover, and it has no word for someone lost to death.

nodes.label: You have had a fight with your partner
nodes.desc: You and your partner are not speaking, and the Kural says a quarrel is the salt of love, not to be overdone.
nodes.silent: All this is about a lovers’ sulk between two people who love each other, and the friend is speaking for him. It says nothing about a partner who frightens or harms you, and it doesn’t ask you to give way to one.

nodes.label: Your partner reads betrayal into everything
nodes.desc: Every innocent word or act is taken as a sign of someone else. Chapter 132 shows this only as a game between lovers.
keywords: my girlfriend is jealous for no reason
accused of cheating when i didn't
nodes.silent: Chapter 132 shows this only as love play: she has no real cause, and her love runs over. It offers no way through, and nothing for suspicion that frightens or controls you. Don’t take it as a reason to bear that.

nodes.label: Thinking about how short life is
nodes.desc: Death has come to mind, and the Kural says people can’t be sure of one moment more yet make ten million plans, so do good while you can.
keywords: how long do i have left
