props.quote: Weigh what will be lost, what will be gained, and the profit it will bring later, then act … Look at the finish, the obstacles, and the gain you will reach when it is done, and then act

props.why: No war should begin before it is prepared for: think through every side of it first, and find the ground for a siege first.
props.quote: To march out without thinking through every side of it … Start nothing and scorn no one until you have found the ground for a siege

props.why: What is gained through others’ tears is lost to tears: the tears of those who suffer wear away wealth, and what was taken with tears leaves with tears.
props.quote: are they not the weapon that wears away wealth? … All that was taken with tears leaves with tears

props.why: The world keeps going only because of gentle ways, called kindly regard in one and courtesy in the other.
props.quote: This world exists because of the surpassing beauty called kindly regard … The world goes on because of the courteous

props.why: What lies within shows through: the heart in the face, as crystal shows what is beside it, and something in her adornment, like a thread through a bead.
props.quote: the face shows what is strongest in the heart … Like the thread that shows through a bead, something shows through this young woman’s adornment

props.why: Good speech is wasted on the petty: don’t speak there even by forgetting, since trying to show a man who can’t see leaves you seeing nothing.
props.quote: don’t speak in a petty one, even by forgetting … Whoever tries to show a man who can’t see ends up seeing nothing himself

props.why: Life is not worth buying with disgrace: what would lower you stays forbidden even when your survival depends on it.
props.quote: Even things you can’t do without, give them up if they would lower you … They won’t give up shame for life

props.why: Goodness decides what poverty does: with worth there is no disgrace, without righteousness a man is a stranger even to the mother who bore him.
props.quote: Having nothing is no disgrace, if you have the strength called worth … looked at as a stranger, even by the mother who bore him

props.why: Tenderness itself has become a warning: she cannot enjoy his embrace or his kindness for fear that he means to leave.
props.quote: Now our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave … He comforts me so fully and joins me so gladly, but in it I see myself bearing pain again

props.why: Having him brings no relief: the fear of losing him spoils the very moment of having him.
props.quote: Now our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave … when it has him it fears parting

props.why: Her slipped bangles do the telling: what her arms have lost tells everyone that he has gone, and how cruel he is.
props.quote: Won’t these bangles slipping from my forearm spread the word … Your arms, their bangles gone and their old beauty withered, tell of the cruelty of a cruel man

props.why: The real test is holding back where your anger could do damage, not where it can’t reach.
props.quote: holds back anger where it can take effect

props.why: Says to keep anger out even of your thoughts, and that all you have set your mind on then comes.
props.quote: never even think of anger in your heart

props.why: Holding back anger goes with learning and restraint here, and righteousness comes looking for such a person.
props.quote: holds back anger, learns and keeps restraint

props.why: Makes a heart free of envy a rule of conduct to be held to.
props.quote: keep your heart free of envy

props.why: Being free of envy towards everyone is ranked with the greatest of blessings.
props.quote: If you can be free of envy towards everyone

props.why: Knowing the harm of a bad path is what holds people back from acting on envy.
props.quote: do nothing unrighteous out of envy

props.why: Envy has never raised anyone, and having none of it has never cost anyone their prosperity.
props.quote: No one has grown great through envy

props.why: Suffering clings to those who cling, and doesn’t let go of them.
props.quote: Suffering holds on and won’t let go

props.why: Where craving is, suffering keeps coming, one after another, with no end.
props.quote: suffering comes on and on, without end

props.why: Says that each thing you let go of is one thing that can no longer cause you pain.
props.quote: you suffer no more pain

props.why: Says the sorrow in the mind is hard to remove without reaching the feet of the one who has no equal.
props.quote: the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove

props.why: Promises no suffering, ever, to those who reach the feet of the one who wants nothing and rejects nothing.
props.quote: will have no suffering, ever

props.why: Not craving pleasure, and calling suffering natural, is what keeps sorrow from coming.
props.quote: says suffering is natural

props.why: Says to cherish and keep close the people who can end a suffering that has come.
props.quote: those who can end the suffering that has come

props.why: Craving is named as the seed of birth that never ends, for every living thing.
props.quote: craving is the seed that yields

props.why: Each loss makes gambling more loved, not less, and the soul goes the same way with pain.
props.quote: gambling is loved more with each loss

props.why: He hears his heart’s hope of joining one who lets a sulk wither, and calls it what it is.
props.quote: That is only craving

props.why: Cutting craving off completely is the step named, and deeds that never fail you follow.
props.quote: If you cut off craving completely

props.why: Giving up what can never be filled gives you, at that very moment, a nature that doesn’t change.
props.quote: If you give up craving

props.why: The free are defined as those free of craving. No one else is free in the same way.
props.quote: the ones free of craving

props.why: Having no craving is called purity, and it comes from wanting truthfulness.
props.quote: Purity is having no craving

props.why: A single possession is enough to bring the old confusion back.
props.quote: Owning even one thing brings back delusion

props.why: Those who haven’t let go completely are pictured as deluded and caught in a net.
props.quote: deluded, and caught in a net

props.why: Hold on to the one who holds on to nothing, as the way to let go of everything else.
props.quote: so that you can let go of attachment

props.why: Letting go can go thing by thing, and each one let go stops being a source of pain.
props.quote: From each thing you have let go of

props.why: Know what to rest on and live so that attachment dies, and the ills on their way to you won’t come.
props.quote: live so that attachment dies

props.why: Not clinging at the moment of gain is what spares you the grief of loss.
props.quote: never clung to what they gained

props.why: She tells a friend who says women like her can cross it that desire is a real sea.
props.quote: There is indeed a sea of desire

props.why: Desire sweeps away shame and strength together, the very raft that should carry you.
props.quote: The fierce flood of desire carries off the raft

props.why: Gossip and a mother’s words only feed it, like manure and water on a plant.
props.quote: this sickness grows on

props.why: Trying to shame desire away with gossip only feeds it, as ghee feeds a fire.
props.quote: put out a fire with ghee

props.why: Desire can intoxicate on a thought or a glance, which toddy can’t do.
props.quote: To be drunk at a thought and elated at a glance

props.why: Her heart can go to him and her eyes can’t, so they stay behind and swim in tears.
props.quote: swimming in this flood of water

props.why: He is barely on his way when the pallor starts to spread over her.
props.quote: Look here, pallor spreading over my body

props.why: Even a small shift in an embrace is enough to bring the pallor on, thick enough to scoop up.
props.quote: I lay holding him and shifted a little

props.why: Evening brings it on. As the light turns pale, despair buds and pain grows.
props.quote: despair buds in me and pain grows

props.why: With him away, each evening comes to her like strangers to a killing ground.
props.quote: evening comes like strangers to a killing ground

props.why: Evening was only evening until he left.
props.quote: I never knew that evening brings pain

props.why: Her friend sees his unkindness told in her eyes, pale and running with tears.
props.quote: pale and streaming with tears

props.why: Her friend sees it in her body. Her arms waste and her bangles slide off.
props.quote: Now they shrink and the gold bangles slip away

props.why: He said “Don’t be afraid,” and now he is going. She asks if she is to blame for believing him.
props.quote: is there any fault in those who trusted what he swore

props.why: Living among strangers is painful, and parting from those dear to you is worse.
props.quote: More painful still is parting from those dear to you

props.why: The thought of his return makes her heart climb like a plant putting out branches.
props.quote: my heart grows branches and climbs

props.why: All she wants is to look at him until her eyes are full, and then the pallor will go.
props.quote: Let me see my husband until my eyes are full

props.why: One day with him, she says, and she will drink until all this sickness is gone.
props.quote: Let my husband come, just one day

props.why: She is so ready for him that she can’t decide what she will do first when he comes.
props.quote: shall I sulk, shall I embrace him

props.why: He longs too, far off at the ruler’s work, for the win that will let him go home to her.
props.quote: give the evening a feast

props.why: He fears coming too late. If her heart breaks first, what use is it to have her?
props.quote: Once her heart has broken and spilled

props.why: Her eyes’ wanting to see him feels like being eaten.
props.quote: Wanting to see him, they are eating me

props.why: To her, those whose love is returned have the fruit without the stone.
props.quote: the stoneless fruit of desire

props.why: Telling your pain to one who isn’t close to you would be like trying to fill in the sea.
props.quote: Fill in the sea instead

props.why: Her heart pines and still goes after the one who left, and she calls it a fool.
props.quote: You pine because he won’t show tender kindness

props.why: Keeping in her heart one who left and won’t come near only costs her more.
props.quote: we will lose still more of our beauty

props.why: He is so present in her heart that she won’t eat anything hot, in case he burns.
props.quote: My lover lives in my heart

props.why: Just thinking of desire brings a joy that doesn’t fade, which toddy can’t do.
props.quote: even thinking of it brings a great joy

props.why: While he is thinking of the one he loves, there is no pain.
props.quote: When you think of the one you love, no pain comes

props.why: She knows he is always in her heart and can only ask whether she is in his.
props.quote: In mine, oh, he is always there

props.why: Asleep he is on her shoulders, awake he is in her heart. He doesn’t leave her either way.
props.quote: When I wake, he rushes into my heart

props.why: A sneeze that fades makes her wonder if he nearly thought of her, and then didn’t.
props.quote: A sneeze starts to come and then dies away

props.why: She sulks though he has done nothing wrong, because sulking brings out his tenderness.
props.quote: sulking is what draws out his tenderness

props.why: The small hurt of a sulk dims his tenderness for a moment, and it comes back greater.
props.quote: but it comes back greater

props.why: Between two as blended as earth and water, a quarrel is called better than heaven.
props.quote: Is there any heaven better than a lovers’ quarrel

props.why: She sets out to sulk, sees her heart is ready to join him and gives in.
props.quote: I went off meaning to sulk

props.why: Her heart forgets what it came to do and goes to join him instead.
props.quote: my heart forgot that and went to join him

props.why: A sulk is like salt. The right amount helps, and drawing it out spoils things.
props.quote: Drawing it out is like a little too much

props.why: He promises not to part in this life, and she hears that he means to part in the next.
props.quote: her eyes filled with tears

props.why: To her, “I thought of you” can only mean he had forgotten her first.
props.quote: So why did you forget me?

props.why: One glance holds death, an eye and a doe at once, and he can’t separate them.
props.quote: Is it death? Is it an eye? Is it a doe?

props.why: Her eyes, not hidden by her brows, leave him trembling with pain.
props.quote: this trembling pain

props.why: She looks down when he looks, and looks at him when he doesn’t.
props.quote: When I look at her, she looks at the ground

props.why: To him her shy look and modesty are ornament enough.
props.quote: the shy look of a doe

props.why: She can’t carry both, and begs her heart to give up one.
props.quote: give up desire or give up modesty

props.why: Modesty is the bolt on the door, and the axe of desire breaks it down.
props.quote: the door of reserve, bolted with modesty

props.why: Caught up with a heart that can’t forget him, she finds her modesty gone.
props.quote: I have forgotten even my modesty

props.why: When the one she cherishes does all she longs for, modesty is forgotten.
props.quote: we don’t even know there is such a thing as modesty

props.why: Bitterly calls the base fortunate, since they alone have no worry in their hearts.
props.quote: for their hearts have no worries

props.why: Even in a sulk there is a worry working away: will this delay coming together?
props.quote: the worry over whether union will be delayed

props.why: Yesterday’s want was almost too much, and the first thought today is whether it will come again.
props.quote: Will it come today too

props.why: Sleep is possible even in a fire, but not with poverty on your mind.
props.quote: In poverty there is no sleep at all

props.why: Says the sorrow of the mind is hard to shift unless you reach the feet of the one who has no equal.
props.quote: the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove

props.why: Says the way to meet what is to come is to guard against it, and then nothing comes to shake you.
props.quote: have no suffering that comes and shakes them

props.why: However strong the walls, being afraid leaves you with no fort.
props.quote: There is no fort for those who are afraid

props.why: A ruler with no defences ready takes fright when war comes, and quickly falls.
props.quote: will take fright when it does

props.why: Size and sharp tusks don’t stop an elephant being afraid when a tiger comes.
props.quote: yet it fears a tiger’s attack

props.why: Fear of the assembly can keep all you have learned from being said, as if you weren’t there.
props.quote: Those who fear the assembly

props.why: Some fear is wisdom. Fearing what should be feared is called the way of those who understand.
props.quote: To fear what should be feared

props.why: Fear of speaking before others is met by learning well beforehand.
props.quote: so that you can answer in an assembly without fear

props.why: After a lie it is your own heart, knowing what it knows, that does the burning.
props.quote: your own heart will burn you

props.why: No outward look helps when your own heart is sinking into a fault you know is yours.
props.quote: your own heart sinks into what you know is a fault

props.why: What is done against what has been forbidden brings pain later, even when it works.
props.quote: brings pain even if it succeeds

props.why: Once it is done, says not to do the like again. Parimelazhagar hears “don’t go on grieving”.
props.quote: it is good not to do the like again

props.why: Tending living beings and holding to compassion leaves you with no deeds that frighten your own soul.
props.quote: no deeds that make their own soul afraid

props.why: Scorn stings even when it is meant as a joke.
props.quote: Scorn hurts, even in fun

props.why: A single word of refusal is enough to take the life out of someone who has had to beg.
props.quote: the life goes out of those who beg

props.why: States it flatly: those with nothing are scorned and the rich are honoured.
props.quote: Everyone scorns those who have nothing

props.why: Poverty can bring even those of good family to say what shames them.
props.quote: poverty brings a weakness from which shameful words are born

props.why: The blame falls on her for turning pale, and no one says what he has done.
props.quote: No one says, “He has left her.”

props.why: People laugh in front of her because they have never suffered what she has.
props.quote: Fools laugh in front of my eyes

props.why: Having nothing isn’t itself the disgrace, if you have the strength called worth.
props.quote: Having nothing is no disgrace

props.why: Following those who despise you brings neither fame nor the land of the gods, so why do it?
props.quote: why follow behind those who despise you

props.why: Says to hold yourself higher, not lower, when your means shrink.
props.quote: When your means shrink, stand tall

props.why: Where you have been put doesn’t settle what you are. Those who aren’t low aren’t made low by it.
props.quote: Those who aren’t low aren’t low, even sitting low

props.why: Gruel as thin as water, from your own labour, is called sweeter than anything.
props.quote: nothing is sweeter than eating what your own labour has brought

props.why: Lacking good fortune shames no one. Disgrace lies only in knowing what must be done and making no effort.
props.quote: The lack of a favouring fate disgraces no one

props.why: Regret arrives with the blow, when it is too late to guard against what could have been prevented.
props.quote: will regret that mistake when the blow lands

props.why: Hidden wrongdoing brings trouble after trouble, until the cry comes: what have we done?
props.quote: until they cry “What have we done?”

props.why: She agreed to his leaving, can’t bear it now, and has no one to tell.
props.quote: I agreed to go without the kindness

props.why: Her eyes looked first and understood later, and now they suffer for it.
props.quote: looked without knowing what would come

props.why: If you have done what makes you cry out, don’t do the like again. Parimelazhagar hears “don’t go on grieving”.
props.quote: it is good not to do the like again

props.why: Living among people who aren’t your own is named as a pain, before she even gets to parting.
props.quote: It is painful to live in a town without your own people

props.why: When everyone else sleeps, she is the only one awake.
props.quote: Even at midnight I alone am here

props.why: All living things are asleep, and the night and she are left with each other.
props.quote: has no companion but me

props.why: Alone with her thoughts, she finds her own heart stays only to eat at her.
props.quote: When I sat alone and thought

props.why: Deserted even by her own heart, she asks if it is because the ruined have no friends.
props.quote: the ruined have no friends

props.why: Being alone is called better than calling your own those who fail you when it counts.
props.quote: Better to be alone

props.why: Says where friendship comes from: loving-kindness makes you warm towards people, and the warmth brings it.
props.quote: that warmth brings friendship

props.why: Words leave a scar that stays after a burn from fire has healed.
props.quote: A scar burned by the tongue never heals

props.why: Being deserted in your ruin goes on burning, even when you think of it at the hour of death.
props.quote: desert you in your ruin burns the heart

props.why: She asks what people could do as enemies, if this is the suffering they bring as friends.
props.quote: bring suffering even in friendship

props.why: Friends whose acts and words don’t match leave a bitterness that reaches you even in a dream.
props.quote: bitter even in a dream

props.why: A friend who doesn’t agree at heart is an anvil. When they find their chance, you are what gets struck.
props.quote: you are struck on it

props.why: Says not to take on friends who cut away your strength in trouble.
props.quote: Don’t take the friendship of those who cut away your strength

props.why: Says to leave friends who don’t fit, even if it costs you something to get free.
props.quote: leave the friendship of those who don’t fit

props.why: Those who are warm in private and blame you in public are to be kept away altogether.
props.quote: come near you at all

props.why: Doubting someone you have come to trust is named as a suffering that doesn’t end.
props.quote: to doubt someone you have come to trust

props.why: Suspicion, once in place, is very hard for anyone to clear.
props.quote: Once suspicion has set in

props.why: Even those who understand can sometimes leave, so she can’t rest on anyone’s word.
props.quote: It is hard to trust

props.why: Living with those who aren’t of one mind with you is like sharing a hut with a snake.
props.quote: sharing a hut with a snake

props.why: Trust follows testing, and goes only as far as the testing showed.
props.quote: After testing, trust them with what they can be trusted with

props.why: Look at a person’s good points and faults together, and judge by which are more.
props.quote: see which are more, and judge them by that

props.why: A person’s own deeds are what to test them by.
props.quote: their own deeds are the touchstone

props.why: Names the moment itself: the thought that this is too hard.
props.quote: Don’t lose heart and say “This is too hard.”

props.why: The answer to “too hard” is effort, which gives you the greatness to finish.
props.quote: Effort will give you greatness

props.why: A flood of trouble dies away once a wise person sets their mind to it.
props.quote: Even a flood of trouble dies away

props.why: Those who won’t be troubled by trouble turn it back on itself.
props.quote: will give trouble trouble

props.why: Keep going like an ox through every blocked place, and the trouble is what gets into trouble.
props.quote: pulls through every blocked place

props.why: Stay unbroken, and even troubles that pile up are the ones in trouble.
props.quote: Even if they come heaped one on another

props.why: Aiming high keeps its worth even when it falls short.
props.quote: Even when it fails, it has the nature of not failing

props.why: Missing something great is called better than hitting something small.
props.quote: a spear that missed an elephant

props.why: Struck by a mass of arrows, an elephant stands its ground, and so do the strong when things fall apart.
props.quote: The strong don’t falter when things fall apart

props.why: Says to keep your mind off what makes your spirit shrink.
props.quote: Don’t think of things that make your spirit small

props.why: What you have listened to becomes a prop when you falter.
props.quote: a prop to lean on when you falter

props.why: Says to stay resolute in work that brings joy, even when great pain comes.
props.quote: Even if great pain comes, be resolute

props.why: People who suffer and can’t bear it have their tears, and those tears are called a weapon that wears away wealth.
props.quote: those who suffer and can’t bear it

props.why: Whatever way round it you plan, fate is there ahead of you.
props.quote: Even as you plan a way around it, it gets there first

props.why: She can see the sea she is in, and no raft to cross it.
props.quote: There is no safe raft to cross it

props.why: She swims on and no shore comes into sight.
props.quote: and see no shore

props.why: With nothing left, she asks her own heart to think of any cure at all.
props.quote: any cure at all for this unending sickness

props.why: Even where the result is denied, the effort still pays its wages.
props.quote: effort pays the wages of your body’s toil

props.why: Where action isn’t possible, the next step is to look for the way that will work.
props.quote: look for the way that will work and do that

props.why: Knowing the body is a target for suffering is what stops turmoil being taken as distress.
props.quote: don’t treat the turmoil that comes on them as distress

props.why: Her eyes can’t sleep when he stays away and can’t sleep when he comes.
props.quote: When he comes they don’t sleep

props.why: Desire gives her heart no rest, keeping it at work in the dead of night.
props.quote: Even in the dead of night it rules my heart

props.why: Her desire can’t stay still. It wanders the streets in a daze, thinking no one knows.
props.quote: wanders the streets in a daze

props.why: Unsure of one more moment, people still run through thoughts by the ten million.
props.quote: they think thoughts by the ten million

props.why: However little he cherished her, her eyes can’t rest without seeing him.
props.quote: my eyes will not rest until they see him

props.why: A good person’s poverty is this: not being able to settle when they can’t do what they must.
props.quote: being unable to rest when they can’t do what they must

props.why: Understanding is what stops the mind going wherever it goes, and turns it from evil to good.
props.quote: doesn’t let the mind go wherever it goes

props.why: Great delight can bring a carelessness called worse than boundless rage.
props.quote: the high spirits of great delight

props.why: Names the moment when delight starts to feel like strength.
props.quote: When your delight makes you feel strong

props.why: A fool with something of their own in hand is compared to a madman getting drunk.
props.quote: like a madman getting drunk

props.why: At the height of delight, the thing to do is call to mind those neglect has ruined.
props.quote: remember those who were ruined by neglect

props.why: Holding back anger is named with restraint as what brings righteousness to you.
props.quote: holds back anger, learns and keeps restraint

props.why: Anger is one of four things that righteousness is defined as being free of.
props.quote: righteousness is a life free of these four

props.why: Keeping the heart free of envy is itself to be taken as the rule of conduct.
props.quote: Make it your rule of conduct

props.why: Envy heads the list of four things that righteousness is a life free of.
props.quote: righteousness is a life free of these four

props.why: Holding to compassion is set against misery, with the earth itself called as witness.
props.quote: Those who hold to compassion have no misery

props.why: Friendship is defined by what it does with pain: it shares it when ruin comes and takes trouble away at once.
props.quote: shares the pain when ruin comes

props.why: Wanting nothing is set above all wealth, against the craving that is never filled.
props.quote: no great wealth here to match wanting nothing

props.why: Fearing craving is called righteousness, and craving is one of four things righteousness is free of.
props.quote: To fear it is righteousness

props.why: Renouncing completely is set against being caught in the net of those who hold on.
props.quote: Those who renounce completely have arrived

props.why: Knowing what to rest on, in the chapter on truth, is what lets attachment die.
props.quote: live so that attachment dies

props.why: The feet of the one who has no equal are named as what removes the sorrow of the mind.
props.quote: the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove

props.why: Guarding against what is to come is set against the suffering that comes and shakes you.
props.quote: guard against what is to come

props.why: Learning is set against fear of the assembly: learn well so that you can answer without fear.
props.quote: Learn by the right path

props.why: Holding to compassion is what leaves a person with no deeds their own soul fears.
props.quote: no deeds that make their own soul afraid

props.why: Worth is named as the strength that keeps having nothing from being a disgrace.
props.quote: the strength called worth

props.why: Keeping your actions clean is what spares you the cry of “What have I done?”
props.quote: Don’t do what will make you cry

props.why: Testing is set against doubt: trusting the untested and doubting the tested both bring suffering.
props.quote: Trust no one without testing them

props.why: Chapter 63 sets staying unbroken against trouble: heaped troubles that reach such a person are themselves in trouble.
props.quote: the troubles that reach an unbroken person are themselves in trouble

props.why: Effort is the answer given to the thought that something is too hard.
props.quote: Effort will give you greatness

props.why: Thinking of rising higher is said to keep its worth even when it fails.
props.quote: Let all your thoughts be of rising higher

props.why: Listening is named as the prop that holds you up when you falter.
props.quote: a prop to lean on when you falter

props.why: Effort is set against fate itself: even where god won’t allow the result, it pays its wages.
props.quote: effort pays the wages of your body’s toil

props.why: Remembering those ruined by neglect is what keeps delight from turning into carelessness.
props.quote: remember those who were ruined by neglect

props.why: Being let down by someone close can hurt more than the same thing from a stranger.
Afterwards it can be hard to know how far to believe them.
One side of the book: leave the friendship of those who don’t fit, even at a cost, and don’t take those who cut away your strength.
props.quote: leave the friendship of those who don’t fit

props.why: The other side: the world wants those who don’t give up a friendship that has come down unbroken.
props.quote: don’t give up the friendship

props.why: Being left when things got hard can hurt long after the trouble itself has passed.
With people gone from your side, a hard time can also become a lonely one.
Says ruin has one benefit: it measures your people, and those who leave when it stops paying were never much to gain or lose.
props.quote: a rod that measures your people to their full length

props.why: Says being alone is better than calling your own those who fail you when it counts, though Parimelazhagar adds that being alone is bad too.
props.quote: Better to be alone

props.why: Opening up to someone new can bring doubt about what they really want.
Says to test first, by character, family, faults and the people around them, and then to trust only as far as the test showed.
props.quote: Trust no one without testing them

props.why: You may start to doubt whether the people around you are good for you.
Stepping back from the people you know can feel lonely.
Says your understanding takes on the nature of your company, as water takes on the nature of the ground it meets.
props.quote: understanding takes on the nature of their company

props.why: Says to leave friends who don’t fit, even if it costs you something to get clear of them.
props.quote: leave the friendship of those who don’t fit

props.why: Once smiles and deeds stop matching, it can be hard to believe anything they say.
Not knowing when the blow will come can keep you on your guard.
Harm can hurt more when it comes from someone acting like a friend.
Says this is something to be afraid of, and that fearing what should be feared is the way of those who understand.
props.quote: Fear the deceivers who smile sweetly

props.why: Says those who aren’t with you in their minds aren’t to be trusted on what they say alone.
props.quote: on their words alone

props.why: Says to keep those who are warm in private and blame you in public from coming near you at all.
props.quote: come near you at all

props.why: Being told what you didn’t want to hear can sting, most of all from someone close.
A first reaction can be anger at the person who said it.
Says friends are made to step in and rebuke you when you go too far, and that those who do are your protection.
props.quote: companions who will rebuke you

props.why: Asks you to look for the reality in what was said, whoever said it.
props.quote: seeing the reality in it

props.why: A friend’s trouble can stay on your mind, and you may not know what would help.
Says friendship moves at once, like a hand to slipping clothes, and shares the pain when ruin comes.
props.quote: friendship takes away trouble on the spot

props.why: Not knowing which way to go can keep the mind turning.
It can be hard to know whose guidance to believe.
Says to choose with care the friendship of the wise, and calls making the great your own the rarest of rare things.
props.quote: choose with care the friendship of the wise

props.why: Calls the words of people of good conduct a staff on slippery ground, and says even a little listening brings greatness.
props.quote: like a staff on slippery ground

props.why: Being hurt or insulted can bring a strong urge to hit back.
Under the wish to hit back there is often the wound itself.
Says not to plot another’s ruin, because the harm you do comes back to you by itself.
props.quote: harm will come to you in the afternoon

props.why: Says to guard against anger for your own sake, because it kills your smile and your joy.
props.quote: it is you that anger kills

props.why: Someone’s words or actions can bring anger on fast, before you have chosen it.
Anger often has a hurt underneath it.
Says to guard against anger for your own sake: it kills the one who holds it and burns the raft that is your own people.
props.quote: it is you that anger kills

props.why: Being provoked again and again can wear down the calmest temper.
Not knowing when the next clash will come can stay on your mind.
Says turning aside from strife brings gain, and that if you press on with it, ruin presses on towards you.
props.quote: Turning aside from strife brings gain

props.why: Seeing someone else do well can bring a pain that is hard to admit.
Says to keep your heart free of envy, since no one has ever grown great through it.
props.quote: No one has grown great through envy

props.why: Seeing what your words did can leave your own heart burning.
It is common to go back over the moment and wish it unsaid.
Says a scar burned by the tongue never heals, so whatever else you fail to guard, guard your tongue.
props.quote: A scar burned by the tongue never heals

props.why: Once it is done, the words say not to do the like again, and Parimelazhagar reads them as: don’t go on grieving.
props.quote: it is good not to do the like again

props.why: Says that seeking out what is good and saying it sweetly makes wrongs wear away.
props.quote: wrongs will wear away and righteousness will grow

props.why: Easy money can start to look like something you need.
Says deep poverty with worth is better than prosperity gained by disgrace, and that such wealth won’t hold, like water in raw clay.
props.quote: Better the deep poverty of the worthy

props.why: Says to let go at once of any gain that comes from leaving the middle, even if it brings only good.
props.quote: let go at once of gain that comes from leaving the middle

props.why: Answers the plea of being short: do evil because you are poor, and you will be poor again.
props.quote: Don’t do evil because you are poor

props.why: Even before you have spoken, the thought of lying can sit badly with your own heart.
Its test is harm: truthfulness is speech with no harm in it, and a lie counts as truthfulness only if it brings good with no fault.
props.quote: speech with no harm in it

props.why: Desire doesn’t always ask first whether it is free to go where it goes.
Knowing who else would be hurt can weigh on you.
Says that whatever else you do wrong, this is the line to keep, speaking of a man and another man’s wife.
props.quote: it is good not to crave

props.why: Names four things that never leave the one who crosses this line: enmity, sin, fear and blame.
props.quote: these four never leave

props.why: Having to bow to those who scorn you can lower you in your own eyes.
Scorn can hurt, even when it is passed off as nothing.
Says where you have been put doesn’t settle what you are.
props.quote: Those who aren’t low aren’t low, even sitting low

props.why: Asks what following those who despise you has ever won, and says those who want strength of character won’t do what is unworthy.
props.quote: why follow behind those who despise you

props.why: Knowing what you did can leave your own heart burning, even if no one else knows.
It is common to keep going back over it and asking “What have I done?”
Once it is done, the words say not to do the like again, and Parimelazhagar reads them as: don’t go on grieving.
props.quote: it is good not to do the like again

props.why: Says that seeking out what is good and saying it sweetly makes wrongs wear away.
props.quote: wrongs will wear away

props.why: Doing good work and not being seen can hurt, most of all when others are praised.
With no word of thanks, it can be hard to keep caring about the work.
Says a person’s own deeds are the touchstone, and not to scorn anyone for how they look, since some are the axle pin of the chariot.
props.quote: their own deeds are the touchstone

props.why: Says effort isn’t wasted: it pays its wages even where the result is denied.
props.quote: effort pays the wages of your body’s toil

props.why: A task that looks too big can sink your spirit before you have begun.
Says not to lose heart and call it too hard, because effort gives greatness, and to take care not to let the work fail.
props.quote: Effort will give you greatness

props.why: Says to know what you can do before you go, since many set out on a surge of zeal and broke halfway.
props.quote: know what they can do

props.why: Says to stay resolute in work that brings joy, even when great pain comes.
props.quote: be resolute and do the work

props.why: After a real effort comes to nothing, it can be hard to believe the next one is worth making.
It is common to go back over what you might have done differently.
Says aiming high keeps its worth even when it fails, and that a spear that missed an elephant beats an arrow that hit a hare.
props.quote: Even when it fails, it has the nature of not failing

props.why: Says lacking a favouring fate disgraces no one, and that effort pays its wages even where the result is denied.
props.quote: The lack of a favouring fate disgraces no one

props.why: Offers the picture of an elephant struck by a mass of arrows that still stands its ground.
props.quote: The strong don’t falter when things fall apart

props.why: Knowing something needs doing and not doing it can keep the mind from settling.
Says that once you have settled on a task, don’t waver or delay, and to take your time only over what should go slowly.
props.quote: don’t waver or delay

props.why: Says not to put good off to some other day, and to do it before the tongue is stilled.
props.quote: see to it some other day

props.why: When trouble comes from every side, it can be hard to keep your spirit up.
With so much wrong at once, it can be hard to see a way out.
Each new trouble can leave you waiting for the next one.
Says to keep close those who can end a suffering that has come, and that friendship shares the pain when ruin comes.
props.quote: those who can end the suffering that has come

props.why: Says to act where you can, and where you can’t, to look for the way that will work.
props.quote: look for the way that will work

props.why: Its own answer is to stay unbroken, so that troubles heaped on one another are the ones in trouble.
props.quote: Even if they come heaped one on another

props.why: Risking money or years on something uncertain can keep you turning it over.
A new plan can bring high spirits that feel like strength.
Says to weigh loss, gain and later profit first, and not to start what looks for profit and loses the capital.
props.quote: Weigh what will be lost, what will be gained

props.why: Says to look at the finish, the obstacles and the gain you will reach, and then act.
props.quote: Look at the finish, the obstacles

props.why: Says to weigh the task, your own strength and the strength of those for and against you before you act.
props.quote: the strength of the task, your own strength

props.why: Too many things at once can leave you always thinking of the one you haven’t done.
When the load keeps growing, your spirit can start to give way.
Says even peacock feathers will break an axle if you pile them too high, and that the tip of a branch is no place to climb further.
props.quote: if you pile them too high

props.why: Says to work out who can finish a task and by what means, and then leave it in their hands.
props.quote: leave it in their hands

props.why: Not knowing whether to act or wait can keep the mind going back and forth.
Says to hold still like the heron, unshaken, and when your moment comes to be like its strike.
props.quote: In the time for holding still, be like the heron

props.why: Says deliberation ends in a decision, and that leaving a decision to sit in delay is wrong.
props.quote: The end of deliberation is to reach a decision

props.why: Choosing someone can bring doubt about whether they will do what they say.
Says work goes to one who knows how and can endure to the end, not to a favourite, and once judged, leave it in their hands.
props.quote: Work is not something to hand to a favourite

props.why: Those who answer to you can try your patience, and anger comes easily where it can take effect.
Being obeyed can bring high spirits that feel like strength.
Says that when you go against those weaker than you, think of yourself before those stronger, and don’t do what you know is painful.
props.quote: think of yourself before those stronger

props.why: Says holding back anger only counts where it can take effect, which is where you hold power.
props.quote: holds back anger where it can take effect

props.why: Says of a ruler to look into a wrong fairly first, and that harsh words and punishment past all measure wear away his strength.
props.quote: Harsh words and punishment past all measure

props.why: When your living depends on someone’s mood, being near them can be frightening.
It can be hard to stop thinking about what they might do next.
A minister’s rule near a quarrelsome ruler: as with a fire, stay neither too far nor too near, and don’t presume on favour.
props.quote: neither too far nor too near

props.why: Sets a limit: even when in trouble, those of unshaken vision won’t do anything shameful.
props.quote: won’t do anything shameful

props.why: Facing someone with more power can bring fear, whatever you tell yourself.
Not knowing what they will do next can stay on your mind.
Says to weigh the task, your own strength, theirs and your allies’ before you act.
props.quote: the strength of the task, your own strength

props.why: Says even the weak can win if they know the place and guard themselves, and that a great force loses heart on ground that suits the small.
props.quote: Even the weak grow strong and win

props.why: Standing up in front of people can bring fear, even when you know your subject.
Says to learn well beforehand, so that you can answer without fear.
props.quote: so that you can answer in an assembly without fear

props.why: Says to know the assembly, weigh it up and judge the moment before you speak.
props.quote: know the assembly, weigh it up, and then speak

props.why: Saying the same thing to someone who won’t hear it can wear down your temper.
Says whoever tries to show a man who can’t see ends up seeing nothing himself.
props.quote: ends up seeing nothing himself

props.why: Says to save your words for those who can take them in, and before the blank to seem as blank as white lime.
props.quote: take on the colour of white lime

props.why: When things go well, high spirits can start to feel like strength.
Says plenty is the time to bow low, and that in the rich humility is a further wealth.
props.quote: In plenty, bow low

props.why: Says that when delight makes you feel strong, remember those who were ruined by neglect.
props.quote: remember those who were ruined by neglect

props.why: Says prosperity has greatness in it only for those without pride, anger or pettiness.
props.quote: a prosperity with greatness in it

props.why: Watching money go faster than it comes can sit at the back of your mind all day.
Says a narrow way in does no harm as long as the way out is no wider, and that knowing your limit is how to look after wealth as you spend it.
props.quote: as long as the way out is no wider

props.why: When money is short, tomorrow’s needs can be hard to put out of your mind, even at night.
Having little can bring the feeling of being looked down on, even by people who mean no harm.
Says having nothing is no disgrace if you have the strength called worth, and that when your means shrink you should stand tall.
props.quote: Having nothing is no disgrace

props.why: Says nothing is sweeter than eating what your own labour has brought, even gruel as thin as water.
props.quote: nothing is sweeter than eating what your own labour has brought

props.why: Says those who lose wealth may flower again one day, and counts losing compassion as the worse loss.
props.quote: may flower again one day

props.why: Having to ask can feel like being lowered, even before anyone has answered.
Not knowing what the answer will be, or what you will do without it, can stay with you.
Says to ask those it is right to ask, not those who hide what they have, and that if they hide it the blame is theirs, not yours.
props.quote: the blame is theirs, not yours

props.why: Says having nothing is no disgrace, if you have the strength called worth.
props.quote: Having nothing is no disgrace

props.why: Wanting to help and not being sure you can may keep you from settling.
Says being asked is painful until you see the pleased face of the one who asked, and that those who give without scorn gladden the asker’s heart.
props.quote: until you see the pleased face

props.why: Warns too that helping without weighing what you have will quickly destroy your wealth.
props.quote: Helping others without weighing what you have

props.why: Having money and no one to share it with can feel lonely.
Having enough and still not being at ease can keep the mind turning.
Asks whether those who hoard know the joy of giving and being glad, and says ending hunger is where wealth can be stored.
props.quote: the joy of giving and being glad

props.why: Says the reward of wealth is to live so that your kin gather round you, and that a life with no sharing of hearts is a tank with no bank.
props.quote: so that your kin gather round you

props.why: Says the wealth of one who loves the world is like the village tank filled with water.
props.quote: like the village tank filled with water

props.why: Drink can come to feel needed, even when you can see what it costs.
Drinking in secret, or after promising not to, can leave your heart sinking.
Asks the drinker, sober for a moment, to see a drunk man and think of his own slips, and to give up saying he has never been drunk.
props.quote: doesn’t he think of how he slips

props.why: Each loss can make the next bet feel more necessary, not less.
What has been lost, and who doesn’t know yet, can weigh on you.
Its one counsel is to see the win for what it is, a hook swallowed by a fish, and to see your wealth and income going to others.
props.quote: a hook swallowed by a fish

props.why: Seeing your health change can stay on your mind.
Eating against what you know is good for you can sit badly afterwards.
Says to eat knowing the measure once your food is digested, and that too much or too little both bring disease.
props.quote: eat knowing the measure

props.why: Each new thing can leave you already wanting the next.
Says craving’s nature is never to be filled, and that where it exists, suffering comes on and on.
props.quote: whose nature is never to be filled

props.why: Thinking about what the animal went through can sit uneasily with you.
Says no one would offer flesh for money if the world didn’t kill to eat, and that flesh is another creature’s wound.
props.quote: Flesh is another creature’s wound

props.why: Asks how someone who eats other flesh to swell their own can hold to compassion.
props.quote: hold to compassion

props.why: Wanting to get it right for your children can keep you turning things over.
Says the good a father does his son is to set him in the front rank, and that children who know more than you are sweet.
props.quote: put him in the front rank of the assembly

props.why: A break with your own family can hurt in a way that is hard to explain to others.
Old grievances can come back along with the new one.
Says those who left will come back as kin once the cause of the rift is gone, and that your own people’s ways are bad for you if they do you harm.
props.quote: once the cause of the rift is gone

props.why: Being the one everyone leans on can wear your spirit down over time.
With others depending on you, it can be hard to stop thinking about what comes next.
Says the load falls on those who can carry it, and asks, for them, whether such a body is only a vessel for suffering.
props.quote: the load falls on those who can carry it

props.why: Someone can strike you all at once, before you know anything about them.
Thoughts of them can arrive without being asked.
Part 3 watches for a look that is returned: she looks at the ground, and looks at him when he looks away.
props.quote: she looks at me and softly smiles

props.why: Hearing your private life passed around can hurt, even if it is only talk.
You may keep wondering who knows, and what they will do.
Part 3 says such talk doesn’t end desire but feeds it, as ghee feeds a fire.
props.quote: put out a fire with ghee

props.why: A long absence can wear on you, often worst in the evenings.
You may find yourself counting the days until they are back.
The nights can feel long with no one there.
Says that when you think of the one you love, no pain comes.
props.quote: When you think of the one you love, no pain comes

props.why: Loving someone who doesn’t answer can be a weight you carry alone.
Not being loved back can hurt, even when no one has done anything wrong.
Thinking of sending him word, she tells her heart that telling her pain to one who has drawn away is like trying to fill in the sea.
props.quote: Fill in the sea instead

props.why: Someone gone can stay with you all day, and the mind can keep going back.
Memory can keep you going and burn at the same time.
She tells her own heart that keeping in it one who left only costs her more, and that going after him is foolish.
props.quote: we will lose still more of our beauty

props.why: A fight with the person closest to you can hurt more than the words alone.
In a fight, anger can feel like the only way to be heard.
Her friend, come as his go-between, likens a sulk to salt, good in the right amount and spoiled by drawing it out. It is called sweet only with those who love you.
props.quote: sulking is sweet with those who love you

props.why: Being doubted over small things, when you have done nothing, can hurt.
Being suspected all the time can make a person careful of every word.
Thinking about how little time there is can bring fear, at any age.
The thought can come back at night and keep the mind from settling.
Its answer to how short life is: do good now, for righteousness is the companion that doesn’t die when you die.
props.quote: rush to do good deeds

props.why: Says no one can be sure of one moment more, so do at once the things that stay.
props.quote: do at once the things that stay

props.why: Being worn down can make you want to set everything down.
The thought of leaving can keep coming back and won’t let the mind settle.
Says to keep close those who can end a suffering that has come, and that friendship shares the pain when ruin comes.
props.quote: those who can end the suffering that has come

props.why: Says a home life lived in righteousness, with loving-kindness in it, has nothing to gain from leaving for a renouncer’s path.
props.quote: what would you gain by going off on some outside path

props.why: When one thing after another goes wrong, it can seem that nothing you do will matter.
A long run of bad luck can wear down the will to try again.
Says effort pays the wages of your toil even where the result is denied, and that those who don’t falter will see the back of fate.
props.quote: effort pays the wages of your body’s toil

props.why: Says the lack of a favouring fate disgraces no one, and that in making money what should help can go wrong and what should hurt can turn out well.
props.quote: The lack of a favouring fate disgraces no one

props.why: Giving and getting nothing back can hurt, most of all from those you helped.
After a long time of giving, it can be hard to see why you go on.
Says help given with no thought of return is greater than the sea, and that no one repays the rain.
props.quote: help given with no thought of return

props.why: Warns too that helping others without weighing what you have will quickly destroy your wealth.
props.quote: Helping others without weighing what you have

props.why: You may wonder how you could ever repay it.
Says a good deed done at the right time, though small, is greater than the world, and that those who know its worth hold it so.
props.quote: A good deed done at the right time

props.why: Those raised high by worth, courtesy and the like feel shame at acts unworthy of them.
